rules.author: Oddvar Moe, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community

rules.title: Imports Registry Key From an ADS
rules.description: Detects the import of a alternate datastream to the registry with regedit.exe.
rules.author: Oddvar Moe, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community

rules.title: Regedit as Trusted Installer
rules.description: Detects a regedit started with TrustedInstaller privileges or by ProcessHacker.exe
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Registry Modification From ADS Via Regini.EXE
rules.description: Detects the import of an alternate data stream with regini.exe, regini.exe can be used to modify registry keys.
rules.author: Eli Salem, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community

rules.title: Registry Modification Via Regini.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of regini.exe which can be used to modify registry keys, the changes are imported from one or more text files.
rules.author: Eli Salem, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community

rules.title: DLL Execution Via Register-cimprovider.exe
rules.description: Detects using register-cimprovider.exe to execute arbitrary dll file.
rules.author: Ivan Dyachkov, Yulia Fomina, oscd.community

rules.title: Enumeration for 3rd Party Creds From CLI
rules.description: Detects processes that query known 3rd party registry keys that holds credentials via commandline
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Registry Export of Third-Party Credentials
rules.description:
Detects the use of reg.exe to export registry paths associated with third-party credentials.
Credential stealers have been known to use this technique to extract sensitive information from the registry.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: IE ZoneMap Setting Downgraded To MyComputer Zone For HTTP Protocols Via CLI
rules.description: Detects changes to Internet Explorer's (IE / Windows Internet properties) ZoneMap configuration of the "HTTP" and "HTTPS" protocols to point to the "My Computer" zone. This allows downloaded files from the Internet to be granted the same level of trust as files stored locally.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Debugger Registration Cmdline
rules.description: Detects the registration of a debugger for a program that is available in the logon screen (sticky key backdoor).
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), oscd.community, Jonhnathan Ribeiro

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Logon Scripts - CommandLine
rules.description: Detects the addition of a new LogonScript to the registry value "UserInitMprLogonScript" for potential persistence
rules.author: Tom Ueltschi (@c_APT_ure)

rules.title: Potential Credential Dumping Attempt Using New NetworkProvider - CLI
rules.description: Detects when an attacker tries to add a new network provider in order to dump clear text credentials, similar to how the NPPSpy tool does it
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Python Function Execution Security Warning Disabled In Excel
rules.description:
Detects changes to the registry value "PythonFunctionWarnings" that would prevent any warnings or alerts from showing when Python functions are about to be executed.
Threat actors could run malicious code through the new Microsoft Excel feature that allows Python to run within the spreadsheet.
rules.author: @Kostastsale

rules.title: Potential Privilege Escalation via Service Permissions Weakness
rules.description: Detect modification of services configuration (ImagePath, FailureCommand and ServiceDLL) in registry by processes with Medium integrity level
rules.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov

rules.title: Potential Provisioning Registry Key Abuse For Binary Proxy Execution
rules.description: Detects potential abuse of the provisioning registry key for indirect command execution through "Provlaunch.exe".
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

rules.title: Potential PowerShell Execution Policy Tampering - ProcCreation
rules.description: Detects changes to the PowerShell execution policy registry key in order to bypass signing requirements for script execution from the CommandLine
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Hiding User Account Via SpecialAccounts Registry Key - CommandLine
rules.description: Detects changes to the registry key "HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\SpecialAccounts\Userlist" where the value is set to "0" in order to hide user account from being listed on the logon screen.
rules.author: @Kostastsale, TheDFIRReport

rules.title: Persistence Via TypedPaths - CommandLine
rules.description: Detects modification addition to the 'TypedPaths' key in the user or admin registry via the commandline. Which might indicate persistence attempt
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Regsvr32 Commandline Flag Anomaly
rules.description: Detects a potential command line flag anomaly related to "regsvr32" in which the "/i" flag is used without the "/n" which should be uncommon.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Regsvr32 HTTP IP Pattern
rules.description: Detects regsvr32 execution to download and install DLLs located remotely where the address is an IP address.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Regsvr32 HTTP/FTP Pattern
rules.description: Detects regsvr32 execution to download/install/register new DLLs that are hosted on Web or FTP servers.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Regsvr32 Execution From Remote Share
rules.description: Detects REGSVR32.exe to execute DLL hosted on remote shares
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of Regsvr32
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of "regsvr32.exe".
rules.author: elhoim, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Regsvr32 Execution From Potential Suspicious Location
rules.description: Detects execution of regsvr32 where the DLL is located in a potentially suspicious location.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Regsvr32 Execution From Highly Suspicious Location
rules.description: Detects execution of regsvr32 where the DLL is located in a highly suspicious locations
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Regsvr32 DLL Execution With Suspicious File Extension
rules.description: Detects the execution of REGSVR32.exe with DLL files masquerading as other files
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), frack113

rules.title: Scripting/CommandLine Process Spawned Regsvr32
rules.description: Detects various command line and scripting engines/processes such as "PowerShell", "Wscript", "Cmd", etc. spawning a "regsvr32" instance.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Regsvr32 DLL Execution With Uncommon Extension
rules.description: Detects a "regsvr32" execution where the DLL doesn't contain a common file extension.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - AnyDesk Execution
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly use
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - AnyDesk Piped Password Via CLI
rules.description: Detects piping the password to an anydesk instance via CMD and the '--set-password' flag.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - AnyDesk Execution With Known Revoked Signing Certificate
rules.description:
Detects the execution of an AnyDesk binary with a version prior to 8.0.8.
Prior to version 8.0.8, the Anydesk application used a signing certificate that got compromised by threat actors.
Use this rule to detect instances of older versions of Anydesk using the compromised certificate
This is recommended in order to avoid attackers leveraging the certificate and signing their binaries to bypass detections.

rules.author: Sai Prashanth Pulisetti, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.description: Detects AnyDesk Remote Desktop silent installation. Which can be used by attackers to gain remote access.

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - Potential MeshAgent Execution - Windows
rules.description:
Detects potential execution of MeshAgent which is a tool used for remote access.
Historical data shows that threat actors rename MeshAgent binary to evade detection.
Matching command lines with the '--meshServiceName' argument can indicate that the MeshAgent is being used for remote access.
rules.author: Norbert Jaśniewicz (AlphaSOC)

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - MeshAgent Command Execution via MeshCentral
rules.description:
Detects the use of MeshAgent to execute commands on the target host, particularly when threat actors might abuse it to execute commands directly.
MeshAgent can execute commands on the target host by leveraging win-console to obscure their activities and win-dispatcher to run malicious code through IPC with child processes.
rules.author: @Kostastsale

rules.description:

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - Renamed MeshAgent Execution - Windows
rules.description:
Detects the execution of a renamed instance of the Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tool, MeshAgent.
RMM tools such as MeshAgent are commonly utilized by IT administrators for legitimate remote support and system management.
However, malicious actors may exploit these tools by renaming them to bypass detection mechanisms, enabling unauthorized access and control over compromised systems.
rules.author: Norbert Jaśniewicz (AlphaSOC)

rules.description: Detects ScreenConnect program starts that establish a remote access to a system.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect Remote Command Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a system command via the ScreenConnect RMM service.
rules.author: Ali Alwashali

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect Potential Suspicious Remote Command Execution
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious child processes launched via the ScreenConnect client service.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), @Kostastsale

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect Server Web Shell Execution
rules.description: Detects potential web shell execution from the ScreenConnect server process.
rules.author: Jason Rathbun (Blackpoint Cyber)

rules.description:

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - TacticalRMM Agent Registration to Potentially Attacker-Controlled Server
rules.description:
Detects TacticalRMM agent installations where the --api, --auth, and related flags are used on the command line.
These parameters configure the agent to connect to a specific RMM server with authentication, client ID, and site ID.
This technique could indicate a threat actor attempting to register the agent with an attacker-controlled RMM infrastructure silently.
rules.author: Ahmed Nosir (@egycondor)

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - Team Viewer Session Started On Windows Host
rules.description:
Detects the command line executed when TeamViewer starts a session started by a remote host.
Once a connection has been started, an investigator can verify the connection details by viewing the "incoming_connections.txt" log file in the TeamViewer folder.
rules.author: Josh Nickels, Qi Nan

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - UltraViewer Execution
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly use
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Discovery of a System Time
rules.description: Identifies use of various commands to query a systems time. This technique may be used before executing a scheduled task or to discover the time zone of a target system.
rules.author: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community

rules.title: Renamed AdFind Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of a renamed Adfind.exe. AdFind continues to be seen across majority of breaches. It is used to domain trust discovery to plan out subsequent steps in the attack chain.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Renamed AutoHotkey.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of a renamed autohotkey.exe binary based on PE metadata fields
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali

rules.title: Renamed AutoIt Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of a renamed AutoIt2.exe or AutoIt3.exe.
AutoIt is a scripting language and automation tool for Windows systems. While primarily used for legitimate automation tasks, it can be misused in cyber attacks.
Attackers can leverage AutoIt to create and distribute malware, including keyloggers, spyware, and botnets. A renamed AutoIt executable is particularly suspicious.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Defense Evasion Via Binary Rename

rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Renamed Remote Utilities RAT (RURAT) Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of renamed Remote Utilities (RURAT) via Product PE header field
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Renamed Schtasks Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of renamed schtasks.exe binary, which is a legitimate Windows utility used for scheduling tasks.
One of the very common persistence techniques is schedule malicious tasks using schtasks.exe.
Since, it is heavily abused, it is also heavily monitored by security products. To evade detection, threat actors may rename the schtasks.exe binary to schedule their malicious tasks.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Renamed SysInternals DebugView Execution
rules.description: Detects suspicious renamed SysInternals DebugView execution
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Renamed ProcDump Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of a renamed ProcDump executable.
This often done by attackers or malware in order to evade defensive mechanisms.
rules.detection_summary: {'selection_ofn': {'OriginalFileName': 'procdump'}, 'selection_cli_dump_flag': {'CommandLine|contains|windash': [' -ma ', ' -mp ']}, 'selection_cli_eula_flag': {'CommandLine|contains|windash': ' /accepteula'}, 'filter_main_known_names': {'Image|endswith': ['\\procdump.exe', '\\procdump64.exe']}, 'condition': '(selection_ofn or all of selection_cli_*) and not 1 of filter_main_*'}
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Renamed PsExec Service Execution
rules.description: Detects suspicious launch of a renamed version of the PSEXESVC service with, which is not often used by legitimate administrators
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Renamed Sysinternals Sdelete Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of a renamed SysInternals Sdelete, which is something an administrator shouldn't do (the renaming)

rules.description: Detects renamed vmnat.exe or portable version that can be used for DLL side-loading
rules.author: elhoim

rules.title: Renamed Whoami Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of whoami that has been renamed to a different name to avoid detection
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Capture Credentials with Rpcping.exe
rules.description: Detects using Rpcping.exe to send a RPC test connection to the target server (-s) and force the NTLM hash to be sent in the process.
rules.author: Julia Fomina, oscd.community

rules.title: Ruby Inline Command Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of ruby using the "-e" flag. This is could be used as a way to launch a reverse shell or execute live ruby code.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Rundll32 Execution With DLL Stored In ADS
rules.description: Detects execution of rundll32 where the DLL being called is stored in an Alternate Data Stream (ADS).
rules.author: Harjot Singh, '@cyb3rjy0t'

rules.title: Suspicious Advpack Call Via Rundll32.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "rundll32" calling "advpack.dll" with potential obfuscated ordinal calls in order to leverage the "RegisterOCX" function
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Rundll32 Invoking Inline VBScript
rules.description: Detects suspicious process related to rundll32 based on command line that invokes inline VBScript as seen being used by UNC2452
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Rundll32 InstallScreenSaver Execution
rules.description: An attacker may execute an application as a SCR File using rundll32.exe desk.cpl,InstallScreenSaver
rules.author: Christopher Peacock @securepeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io, TactiKoolSec

rules.title: Suspicious Key Manager Access
rules.description: Detects the invocation of the Stored User Names and Passwords dialogue (Key Manager)
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Mshtml.DLL RunHTMLApplication Suspicious Usage
rules.description: Detects execution of commands that leverage the "mshtml.dll" RunHTMLApplication export to run arbitrary code via different protocol handlers (vbscript, javascript, file, http...)
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems),  Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Josh Nickels, frack113, Zaw Min Htun (ZETA)

rules.title: Rundll32 Execution Without CommandLine Parameters

rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious NTLM Authentication on the Printer Spooler Service
rules.description: Detects a privilege elevation attempt by coercing NTLM authentication on the Printer Spooler service
rules.author: Elastic (idea), Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Obfuscated Ordinal Call Via Rundll32
rules.description: Detects execution of "rundll32" with potential obfuscated ordinal calls
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Rundll32 Spawned Via Explorer.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "rundll32.exe" with a parent process of Explorer.exe. This has been observed by variants of Raspberry Robin, as first reported by Red Canary.
rules.detection_summary: {'selection_parent': {'ParentImage|endswith': '\\explorer.exe'}, 'selection_img': [{'Image|endswith': '\\rundll32.exe'}, {'OriginalFileName': 'RUNDLL32.EXE'}], 'filter_main_generic': [{'CommandLine|contains': ' C:\\Windows\\System32\\'}, {'CommandLine|endswith': ' -localserver 22d8c27b-47a1-48d1-ad08-7da7abd79617'}], 'condition': 'all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_main_*'}
rules.author: CD_ROM_

rules.title: Process Memory Dump Via Comsvcs.DLL
rules.description: Detects a process memory dump via "comsvcs.dll" using rundll32, covering multiple different techniques (ordinal, minidump function, etc.)
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Modexp, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Rundll32 Registered COM Objects
rules.description: load malicious registered COM objects
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Suspicious Process Start Locations
rules.description: Detects suspicious process run from unusual locations
rules.author: juju4, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

rules.title: Suspicious Rundll32 Setupapi.dll Activity
rules.description: setupapi.dll library provide InstallHinfSection function for processing INF files. INF file may contain instructions allowing to create values in the registry, modify files and install drivers. This technique could be used to obtain persistence via modifying one of Run or RunOnce registry keys, run process or use other DLLs chain calls (see references) InstallHinfSection function in setupapi.dll calls runonce.exe executable regardless of actual content of INF file.
rules.author: Konstantin Grishchenko, oscd.community

rules.title: Shell32 DLL Execution in Suspicious Directory
rules.description: Detects shell32.dll executing a DLL in a suspicious directory
rules.author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential ShellDispatch.DLL Functionality Abuse
rules.description: Detects potential "ShellDispatch.dll" functionality abuse to execute arbitrary binaries via "ShellExecute"
rules.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: RunDLL32 Spawning Explorer
rules.description: Detects RunDLL32.exe spawning explorer.exe as child, which is very uncommon, often observes Gamarue spawning the explorer.exe process in an unusual way
rules.author: elhoim, CD_ROM_

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Rundll32 Activity
rules.description: Detects suspicious execution of rundll32, with specific calls to some DLLs with known LOLBIN functionalities
rules.author: juju4, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Control Panel DLL Load
rules.description: Detects suspicious Rundll32 execution from control.exe as used by Equation Group and Exploit Kits

rules.description: Detects the execution of Rundll32.exe with DLL files masquerading as image files

rules.title: Suspicious Usage Of ShellExec_RunDLL
rules.description: Detects suspicious usage of the ShellExec_RunDLL function to launch other commands as seen in the the raspberry-robin attack
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious ShellExec_RunDLL Call Via Ordinal
rules.description:
Detects suspicious call to the "ShellExec_RunDLL" exported function of SHELL32.DLL through the ordinal number to launch other commands.
Adversary might only use the ordinal number in order to bypass existing detection that alert on usage of ShellExec_RunDLL on CommandLine.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

rules.title: ShimCache Flush
rules.description: Detects actions that clear the local ShimCache and remove forensic evidence
rules.detection_summary: {'selection1a': {'CommandLine|contains|all': ['rundll32', 'apphelp.dll']}, 'selection1b': {'CommandLine|contains': ['ShimFlushCache', '#250']}, 'selection2a': {'CommandLine|contains|all': ['rundll32', 'kernel32.dll']}, 'selection2b': {'CommandLine|contains': ['BaseFlushAppcompatCache', '#46']}, 'condition': '( selection1a and selection1b ) or ( selection2a and selection2b )'}
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Rundll32 Activity Invoking Sys File
rules.description: Detects suspicious process related to rundll32 based on command line that includes a *.sys file as seen being used by UNC2452
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Rundll32.EXE Execution of UDL File
rules.description:
Detects the execution of rundll32.exe with the oledb32.dll library to open a UDL file.
Threat actors can abuse this technique as a phishing vector to capture authentication credentials or other sensitive data.
rules.author: @kostastsale

rules.title: Rundll32 UNC Path Execution
rules.description: Detects rundll32 execution where the DLL is located on a remote location (share)
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Rundll32 Execution With Uncommon DLL Extension
rules.description: Detects the execution of rundll32 with a command line that doesn't contain a common extension
rules.author: Tim Shelton, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Yassine Oukessou

rules.title: Suspicious Workstation Locking via Rundll32
rules.description: Detects a suspicious call to the user32.dll function that locks the user workstation
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: WebDav Client Execution Via Rundll32.EXE
rules.description:
Detects "svchost.exe" spawning "rundll32.exe" with command arguments like "C:\windows\system32\davclnt.dll,DavSetCookie".
This could be an indicator of exfiltration or use of WebDav to launch code (hosted on a WebDav server).
rules.author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)

rules.title: Suspicious WebDav Client Execution Via Rundll32.EXE
rules.description: Detects "svchost.exe" spawning "rundll32.exe" with command arguments like C:\windows\system32\davclnt.dll,DavSetCookie. This could be an indicator of exfiltration or use of WebDav to launch code (hosted on WebDav Server) or potentially a sign of exploitation of CVE-2023-23397
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Rundll32 Execution Without Parameters
rules.description: Detects rundll32 execution without parameters as observed when running Metasploit windows/smb/psexec exploit module
rules.author: Bartlomiej Czyz, Relativity

rules.title: Run Once Task Execution as Configured in Registry
rules.description: This rule detects the execution of Run Once task as configured in the registry
rules.author: Avneet Singh @v3t0_, oscd.community, Christopher Peacock @SecurePeacock (updated)

rules.title: Possible Privilege Escalation via Weak Service Permissions
rules.description: Detection of sc.exe utility spawning by user with Medium integrity level to change service ImagePath or FailureCommand
rules.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov

rules.title: New Service Creation Using Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detects the creation of a new service using the "sc.exe" utility.
rules.detection_summary: {'selection': {'Image|endswith': '\\sc.exe', 'CommandLine|contains|all': ['create', 'binPath']}, 'filter_optional_dropbox': {'ParentImage|startswith': ['C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Dropbox\\Client\\', 'C:\\Program Files\\Dropbox\\Client\\'], 'ParentImage|endswith': '\\Dropbox.exe'}, 'condition': 'selection and not 1 of filter_optional_*'}
rules.author: Timur Zinniatullin, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community

rules.title: Service StartupType Change Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detect the use of "sc.exe" to change the startup type of a service to "disabled" or "demand"
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: New Kernel Driver Via SC.EXE
rules.description: Detects creation of a new service (kernel driver) with the type "kernel"
rules.detection_summary: {'selection': {'Image|endswith': '\\sc.exe', 'CommandLine|contains': ['create', 'config'], 'CommandLine|contains|all': ['binPath', 'type', 'kernel']}, 'filter_optional_avira_driver': [{'CommandLine|contains|all': ['create netprotection_network_filter', 'type= kernel start= ', 'binPath= System32\\drivers\\netprotection_network_filter', 'DisplayName= netprotection_network_filter', 'group= PNP_TDI ta
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Interesting Service Enumeration Via Sc.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the enumeration and query of interesting and in some cases sensitive services on the system via "sc.exe".
Attackers often try to enumerate the services currently running on a system in order to find different attack vectors.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

rules.title: Allow Service Access Using Security Descriptor Tampering Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detects suspicious DACL modifications to allow access to a service from a suspicious trustee. This can be used to override access restrictions set by previous ACLs.
rules.detection_summary: {'selection_sc': [{'Image|endswith': '\\sc.exe'}, {'OriginalFileName': 'sc.exe'}], 'selection_sdset': {'CommandLine|contains|all': ['sdset', 'A;']}, 'selection_trustee': {'CommandLine|contains': [';IU', ';SU', ';BA', ';SY', ';WD']}, 'filter_optional_hexnode': {'ParentImage': 'C:\\Hexnode\\Hexnode Agent\\Current\\HexnodeAgent.exe'}, 'condition': 'all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*'}
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Deny Service Access Using Security Descriptor Tampering Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detects suspicious DACL modifications to deny access to a service that affects critical trustees. This can be used to hide services or make them unstoppable.
rules.author: Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

rules.title: Service DACL Abuse To Hide Services Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of the "sc.exe" utility adding a new service with special permission seen used by threat actors which makes the service hidden and unremovable.
rules.author: Andreas Hunkeler (@Karneades)

rules.title: Service Security Descriptor Tampering Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detection of sc.exe utility adding a new service with special permission which hides that service.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Service Path Modification
rules.description: Detects service path modification via the "sc" binary to a suspicious command or path
rules.author: Victor Sergeev, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Persistence Attempt Via Existing Service Tampering
rules.description: Detects the modification of an existing service in order to execute an arbitrary payload when the service is started or killed as a potential method for persistence.
rules.author: Sreeman

rules.title: Stop Windows Service Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detects the stopping of a Windows service via the "sc.exe" utility
rules.author: Jakob Weinzettl, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Schtasks Execution AppData Folder
rules.description: Detects the creation of a schtask that executes a file from C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Local
rules.detection_summary: {'selection': {'Image|endswith': '\\schtasks.exe', 'CommandLine|contains|all': ['/Create', '/RU', '/TR', 'C:\\Users\\', '\\AppData\\Local\\'], 'CommandLine|contains': ['NT AUT', ' SYSTEM ']}, 'filter': {'ParentImage|contains|all': ['\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\', 'TeamViewer_.exe'], 'Image|endswith': '\\schtasks.exe', 'CommandLine|contains': '/TN TVInstallRestore'}, 'condition': 'selection and not fil
rules.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Modification Of Scheduled Tasks
rules.description:
Detects when an attacker tries to modify an already existing scheduled tasks to run from a suspicious location
Attackers can create a simple looking task in order to avoid detection on creation as it's often the most focused on
Instead they modify the task after creation to include their malicious payload
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Scheduled Task Creation Via Schtasks.EXE
rules.description: Detects the creation of scheduled tasks by user accounts via the "schtasks" utility.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation Involving Temp Folder
rules.description: Detects the creation of scheduled tasks that involves a temporary folder and runs only once
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Scheduled Task Creation with Curl and PowerShell Execution Combo
rules.description:
Detects the creation of a scheduled task using schtasks.exe, potentially in combination with curl for downloading payloads and PowerShell for executing them.
This facilitates executing malicious payloads or connecting with C&C server persistently without dropping the malware sample on the host.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Delete Important Scheduled Task
rules.description: Detects when adversaries stop services or processes by deleting their respective scheduled tasks in order to conduct data destructive activities
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Delete All Scheduled Tasks
rules.description: Detects the usage of schtasks with the delete flag and the asterisk symbol to delete all tasks from the schedule of the local computer, including tasks scheduled by other users.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Disable Important Scheduled Task
rules.description: Detects when adversaries stop services or processes by disabling their respective scheduled tasks in order to conduct data destructive activities
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), X__Junior

rules.title: Schedule Task Creation From Env Variable Or Potentially Suspicious Path Via Schtasks.EXE
rules.description: Detects Schtask creations that point to a suspicious folder or an environment variable often used by malware
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Schtasks From Suspicious Folders
rules.description: Detects scheduled task creations that have suspicious action command and folder combinations
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Name As GUID
rules.description: Detects creation of a scheduled task with a GUID like name
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Uncommon One Time Only Scheduled Task At 00:00
rules.description: Detects scheduled task creation events that include suspicious actions, and is run once at 00:00
rules.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential SSH Tunnel Persistence Install Using A Scheduled Task
rules.description: Detects the creation of new scheduled tasks via commandline, using Schtasks.exe. This rule detects tasks creating that call OpenSSH, which may indicate the creation of reverse SSH tunnel to the attacker's server.
rules.author: Rory Duncan

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser
rules.description:
Detects manual execution of the "Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser" task via schtasks.
In order to trigger persistence stored in the "\AppCompatFlags\TelemetryController" registry key.
rules.author: Sreeman

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Powershell Search Order Hijacking - Task
rules.description: Detects suspicious powershell execution via a schedule task where the command ends with an suspicious flags to hide the powershell instance instead of executeing scripts or commands. This could be a sign of persistence via PowerShell "Get-Variable" technique as seen being used in Colibri Loader
rules.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Scheduled Task Executing Payload from Registry
rules.description: Detects the creation of a schtasks that potentially executes a payload stored in the Windows Registry using PowerShell.
rules.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Scheduled Task Executing Encoded Payload from Registry
rules.description: Detects the creation of a schtask that potentially executes a base64 encoded payload stored in the Windows Registry using PowerShell.
rules.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems), @Kostastsale, TheDFIRReport, X__Junior (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Schtasks Schedule Types
rules.description: Detects scheduled task creations or modification on a suspicious schedule type
rules.detection_summary: {'selection_img': [{'Image|endswith': '\\schtasks.exe'}, {'OriginalFileName': 'schtasks.exe'}], 'selection_time': {'CommandLine|contains': [' ONLOGON ', ' ONSTART ', ' ONCE ', ' ONIDLE ']}, 'filter_privs': {'CommandLine|contains': ['NT AUT', ' SYSTEM', 'HIGHEST']}, 'condition': 'all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_*'}
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Schtasks Schedule Type With High Privileges

rules.title: Bad Opsec Defaults Sacrificial Processes With Improper Arguments
rules.description:
Detects attackers using tooling with bad opsec defaults.
E.g. spawning a sacrificial process to inject a capability into the process without taking into account how the process is normally run.
One trivial example of this is using rundll32.exe without arguments as a sacrificial process (default in CS, now highlighted by c2lint), running WerFault without arguments (Kraken - credit am0nsec), and other examples.
rules.author: Oleg Kolesnikov @securonix invrep_de, oscd.community, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Suspicious Browser Launch From Document Reader Process

rules.author: frack113, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Josh Nickels

rules.title: Suspicious ClickFix/FileFix Execution Pattern
rules.description:
Detects suspicious execution patterns where users are tricked into running malicious commands via clipboard manipulation, either through the Windows Run dialog (ClickFix) or File Explorer address bar (FileFix).
Attackers leverage social engineering campaigns—such as fake CAPTCHA challenges or urgent alerts—encouraging victims to paste clipboard contents, often executing mshta.exe, powershell.exe, or similar commands to infect systems.
rules.author: montysecurity, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Explorer Process with Whitespace Padding - ClickFix/FileFix
rules.description:
Detects process creation with suspicious whitespace padding followed by a '#' character, which may indicate ClickFix or FileFix techniques used to conceal malicious commands from visual inspection.
ClickFix and FileFix are social engineering attack techniques where adversaries distribute phishing documents or malicious links that deceive users into opening the Windows Run dialog box or File Explorer search bar.
The victims are then instructed to paste commands from their clipboard, which contain
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Usage of For Loop with Recursive Directory Search in CMD
rules.description:
Detects suspicious usage of the cmd.exe 'for /f' loop combined with the 'tokens=' parameter and a recursive directory listing.
This pattern may indicate an attempt to discover and execute system binaries dynamically, for example powershell, a technique sometimes used by attackers to evade detection.
This behavior has been observed in various malicious lnk files.
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk

rules.title: Potential Command Line Path Traversal Evasion Attempt
rules.description: Detects potential evasion or obfuscation attempts using bogus path traversal via the commandline
rules.author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

rules.description:
Adversaries may acquire credentials from web browsers by reading files specific to the target browser.
Web browsers commonly save credentials such as website usernames and passwords so that they do not need to be entered manually in the future.
Web browsers typically store the credentials in an encrypted format within a credential store.

This is used as an obfuscation and masquerading techniques. Only "perfect" homoglyphs are included; these are characters that
are indistinguishable from ASCII characters and thus may make excellent candidates for homoglyph attack characters.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious JWT Token Search Via CLI
rules.description:
Detects potentially suspicious search for JWT tokens via CLI by looking for the string "eyJ0eX" or "eyJhbG".
JWT tokens are often used for access-tokens across various applications and services like Microsoft 365, Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, and others.
Threat actors may search for these tokens to steal them for lateral movement or privilege escalation.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), kagebunsher

rules.title: Suspicious LNK Command-Line Padding with Whitespace Characters
rules.description:
Detects exploitation of LNK file command-line length discrepancy, where attackers hide malicious commands beyond the 260-character UI limit while the actual command-line argument field supports 4096 characters using whitespace padding (e.g., 0x20, 0x09-0x0D).
Adversaries insert non-printable whitespace characters (e.g., Line Feed \x0A, Carriage Return \x0D) to pad the visible section of the LNK file, pushing malicious commands past the UI-visible boundary.
The hidden payload, executed at runtime
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Local Accounts Discovery
rules.description: Local accounts, System Owner/User discovery using operating systems utilities
rules.author: Timur Zinniatullin, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community

rules.title: LOLBIN Execution From Abnormal Drive
rules.description: Detects LOLBINs executing from an abnormal or uncommon drive such as a mounted ISO.
rules.author: Christopher Peacock '@securepeacock', SCYTHE '@scythe_io', Angelo Violetti - SEC Consult '@angelo_violetti', Aaron Herman

rules.title: LSASS Dump Keyword In CommandLine
rules.description: Detects the presence of the keywords "lsass" and ".dmp" in the commandline, which could indicate a potential attempt to dump or create a dump of the lsass process.
rules.author: E.M. Anhaus, Tony Lambert, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential File Download Via MS-AppInstaller Protocol Handler
rules.description:
Detects usage of the "ms-appinstaller" protocol handler via command line to potentially download arbitrary files via AppInstaller.EXE
The downloaded files are temporarly stored in ":\Users\%username%\AppData\Local\Packages\Microsoft.DesktopAppInstaller_8wekyb3d8bbwe\AC\INetCache\<RANDOM-8-CHAR-DIRECTORY>"
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

rules.title: Suspicious Network Command
rules.description: Adversaries may look for details about the network configuration and settings of systems they access or through information discovery of remote systems
rules.author: frack113, Christopher Peacock '@securepeacock', SCYTHE '@scythe_io'

rules.title: Suspicious Scan Loop Network
rules.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of other systems by IP address, hostname, or other logical identifier on a network that may be used for Lateral Movement from the current system
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Potential Network Sniffing Activity Using Network Tools
rules.description:
Detects potential network sniffing via use of network tools such as "tshark", "windump".
Network sniffing refers to using the network interface on a system to monitor or capture information sent over a wired or wireless connection.
An adversary may place a network interface into promiscuous mode to passively access data in transit over the network, or use span ports to capture a larger amount of data.
rules.author: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Process Launched Without Image Name
rules.description: Detect the use of processes with no name (".exe"), which can be used to evade Image-based detections.
rules.author: Matt Anderson (Huntress)

rules.title: Execution of Suspicious File Type Extension
rules.description:
Detects whether the image specified in a process creation event doesn't refer to an ".exe" (or other known executable extension) file. This can be caused by process ghosting or other unorthodox methods to start a process.
This rule might require some initial baselining to align with some third party tooling in the user environment.
rules.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Non-privileged Usage of Reg or Powershell
rules.description: Search for usage of reg or Powershell by non-privileged users to modify service configuration in registry
rules.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov (idea), Ryan Plas (rule), oscd.community

rules.title: Suspicious Process Patterns NTDS.DIT Exfil
rules.description: Detects suspicious process patterns used in NTDS.DIT exfiltration
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Call To Win32_NTEventlogFile Class
rules.description: Detects usage of the WMI class "Win32_NTEventlogFile" in a potentially suspicious way (delete, backup, change permissions, etc.) from a PowerShell script
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Use Short Name Path in Image
rules.description: Detect use of the Windows 8.3 short name. Which could be used as a method to avoid Image detection
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali

rules.title: Use NTFS Short Name in Command Line
rules.description: Detect use of the Windows 8.3 short name. Which could be used as a method to avoid command-line detection
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Use NTFS Short Name in Image
rules.description: Detect use of the Windows 8.3 short name. Which could be used as a method to avoid Image based detection
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Obfuscated IP Download Activity
rules.description: Detects use of an encoded/obfuscated version of an IP address (hex, octal...) in an URL combined with a download command
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Obfuscated IP Via CLI
rules.description: Detects usage of an encoded/obfuscated version of an IP address (hex, octal, etc.) via command line
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Process Parents
rules.description: Detects suspicious parent processes that should not have any children or should only have a single possible child program
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential PowerShell Execution Via DLL
rules.description:
Detects potential PowerShell execution from a DLL instead of the usual PowerShell process as seen used in PowerShdll.
This detection assumes that PowerShell commands are passed via the CommandLine.
rules.author: Markus Neis, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Privilege Escalation via Named Pipe Impersonation
rules.description: Detects a remote file copy attempt to a hidden network share. This may indicate lateral movement or data staging activity.
rules.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic (idea)

rules.title: Private Keys Reconnaissance Via CommandLine Tools
rules.description: Adversaries may search for private key certificate files on compromised systems for insecurely stored credential
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious RunAs-Like Flag Combination
rules.description: Detects suspicious command line flags that let the user set a target user and command as e.g. seen in PsExec-like tools
rules.detection_summary: {'selection_user': {'CommandLine|contains': [' -u system ', ' --user system ', ' -u NT', ' -u "NT', " -u 'NT", ' --system ', ' -u administrator ']}, 'selection_command': {'CommandLine|contains': [' -c cmd', ' -c "cmd', ' -c powershell', ' -c "powershell', ' --command cmd', ' --command powershell', ' -c whoami', ' -c wscript', ' -c cscript']}, 'condition': 'all of selection*'}
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Windows Processes Suspicious Parent Directory
rules.description: Detect suspicious parent processes of well-known Windows processes
rules.author: vburov

rules.title: Suspicious Program Names
rules.description: Detects suspicious patterns in program names or folders that are often found in malicious samples or hacktools
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Recon Information for Export with Command Prompt
rules.description: Once established within a system or network, an adversary may use automated techniques for collecting internal data.
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Suspicious Process Execution From Fake Recycle.Bin Folder
rules.description: Detects process execution from a fake recycle bin folder, often used to avoid security solution.
rules.author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Redirection to Local Admin Share
rules.description: Detects a suspicious output redirection to the local admins share, this technique is often found in malicious scripts or hacktool stagers
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Registry Modification of MS-settings Protocol Handler
rules.description:
Detects registry modifications to the 'ms-settings' protocol handler, which is frequently targeted for UAC bypass or persistence.
Attackers can modify this registry to execute malicious code with elevated privileges by hijacking the command execution path.
rules.author: frack113, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Remote Desktop Tunneling
rules.description: Detects potential use of an SSH utility to establish RDP over a reverse SSH Tunnel. This can be used by attackers to enable routing of network packets that would otherwise not reach their intended destination.
rules.author: Tim Rauch, Elastic (idea)

rules.title: Potential Defense Evasion Via Right-to-Left Override
rules.description:
Detects the presence of the "u202+E" character, which causes a terminal, browser, or operating system to render text in a right-to-left sequence.
This is used as an obfuscation and masquerading techniques.
rules.author: Micah Babinski, @micahbabinski, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Script Interpreter Execution From Suspicious Folder
rules.description: Detects a suspicious script execution in temporary folders or folders accessible by environment variables
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Script Execution From Temp Folder
rules.description: Detects a suspicious script executions from temporary folder
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems), Tim Shelton

rules.title: Sensitive File Access Via Volume Shadow Copy Backup
rules.description: Detects a command that accesses the VolumeShadowCopy in order to extract sensitive files such as the Security or SAM registry hives or the AD database (ntds.dit)
rules.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems), Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious New Service Creation
rules.description: Detects creation of a new service via "sc" command or the powershell "new-service" cmdlet with suspicious binary paths
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Service Binary Directory
rules.description: Detects a service binary running in a suspicious directory
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Windows Service Tampering
rules.description: Detects the usage of binaries such as 'net', 'sc' or 'powershell' in order to stop, pause, disable or delete critical or important Windows services such as AV, Backup, etc. As seen being used in some ransomware scripts
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), frack113 , X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Shadow Copies Creation Using Operating Systems Utilities
rules.description: Shadow Copies creation using operating systems utilities, possible credential access
rules.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community

rules.title: Shadow Copies Deletion Using Operating Systems Utilities
rules.description: Shadow Copies deletion using operating systems utilities
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Michael Haag, Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community, Andreas Hunkeler (@Karneades)

rules.title: Windows Shell/Scripting Processes Spawning Suspicious Programs
rules.description: Detects suspicious child processes of a Windows shell and scripting processes such as wscript, rundll32, powershell, mshta...etc.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Tim Shelton

rules.title: Process Creation Using Sysnative Folder
rules.description: Detects process creation events that use the Sysnative folder (common for CobaltStrike spawns)
rules.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: System File Execution Location Anomaly
rules.description: Detects the execution of a Windows system binary that is usually located in the system folder from an uncommon location.
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Patrick Bareiss, Anton Kutepov, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious SYSTEM User Process Creation
rules.description: Detects a suspicious process creation as SYSTEM user (suspicious program or command line parameter)
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), David ANDRE (additional keywords)

rules.title: Suspicious SYSVOL Domain Group Policy Access
rules.description: Detects Access to Domain Group Policies stored in SYSVOL
rules.author: Markus Neis, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

rules.title: Tasks Folder Evasion
rules.description:
The Tasks folder in system32 and syswow64 are globally writable paths.
Adversaries can take advantage of this and load or influence any script hosts or ANY .NET Application
in Tasks to load and execute a custom assembly into cscript, wscript, regsvr32, mshta, eventvwr
rules.author: Sreeman

rules.title: Malicious Windows Script Components File Execution by TAEF Detection
rules.description:
Windows Test Authoring and Execution Framework (TAEF) framework allows you to run automation by executing tests files written on different languages (C, C#, Microsoft COM Scripting interfaces
Adversaries may execute malicious code (such as WSC file with VBScript, dll and so on) directly by running te.exe
rules.author: Agro (@agro_sev) oscd.community

rules.title: Malicious PE Execution by Microsoft Visual Studio Debugger
rules.description:
There is an option for a MS VS Just-In-Time Debugger "vsjitdebugger.exe" to launch specified executable and attach a debugger.
This option may be used adversaries to execute malicious code by signed verified binary.
The debugger is installed alongside with Microsoft Visual Studio package.
rules.author: Agro (@agro_sev), Ensar Şamil (@sblmsrsn), oscd.community

rules.title: Suspicious Userinit Child Process
rules.description: Detects a suspicious child process of userinit
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Samir Bousseaden (idea)

rules.title: Suspicious Velociraptor Child Process
rules.description: Detects the suspicious use of the Velociraptor DFIR tool to execute other tools or download additional payloads, as seen in a campaign where it was abused for remote access and to stage further attacks.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Weak or Abused Passwords In CLI
rules.description:
Detects weak passwords or often abused passwords (seen used by threat actors) via the CLI.
An example would be a threat actor creating a new user via the net command and providing the password inline
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Usage Of Web Request Commands And Cmdlets
rules.description: Detects the use of various web request commands with commandline tools and Windows PowerShell cmdlets (including aliases) via CommandLine
rules.author: James Pemberton / @4A616D6573, Endgame, JHasenbusch, oscd.community, Austin Songer @austinsonger

rules.title: WhoAmI as Parameter
rules.description: Detects a suspicious process command line that uses whoami as first parameter (as e.g. used by EfsPotato)
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Execution via WorkFolders.exe
rules.description: Detects using WorkFolders.exe to execute an arbitrary control.exe
rules.author: Maxime Thiebaut (@0xThiebaut)

rules.title: Suspect Svchost Activity
rules.description: It is extremely abnormal for svchost.exe to spawn without any CLI arguments and is normally observed when a malicious process spawns the process and injects code into the process memory space.
rules.author: David Burkett, @signalblur

rules.title: Suspicious Process Masquerading As SvcHost.EXE
rules.description:
Detects a suspicious process that is masquerading as the legitimate "svchost.exe" by naming its binary "svchost.exe" and executing from an uncommon location.
Adversaries often disguise their malicious binaries by naming them after legitimate system processes like "svchost.exe" to evade detection.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

rules.title: Terminal Service Process Spawn
rules.description: Detects a process spawned by the terminal service server process (this could be an indicator for an exploitation of CVE-2019-0708)
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Uncommon Svchost Command Line Parameter
rules.description:
Detects instances of svchost.exe running with an unusual or uncommon command line parameter by excluding known legitimate or common patterns.
This could point at a file masquerading as svchost, a process injection, or hollowing of a legitimate svchost instance.
rules.author: Liran Ravich

rules.title: Uncommon Svchost Parent Process
rules.description: Detects an uncommon svchost parent process
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Permission Check Via Accesschk.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of the "Accesschk" utility, an access and privilege audit tool developed by SysInternal and often being abused by attacker to verify process privileges
rules.author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov (idea), Mangatas Tondang, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Active Directory Database Snapshot Via ADExplorer
rules.description: Detects the execution of Sysinternals ADExplorer with the "-snapshot" flag in order to save a local copy of the active directory database. This can be used by attackers to extract data for Bloodhound, usernames for password spraying or use the meta data for social engineering. The snapshot doesn't contain password hashes but there have been cases, where administrators put passwords in the comment field.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Active Directory Database Snapshot Via ADExplorer
rules.description: Detects the execution of Sysinternals ADExplorer with the "-snapshot" flag in order to save a local copy of the active directory database to a suspicious directory. This can be used by attackers to extract data for Bloodhound, usernames for password spraying or use the meta data for social engineering. The snapshot doesn't contain password hashes but there have been cases, where administrators put passwords in the comment field.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Execution of Sysinternals Tools
rules.description: Detects command lines that contain the 'accepteula' flag which could be a sign of execution of one of the Sysinternals tools
rules.author: Markus Neis

rules.title: Potential Memory Dumping Activity Via LiveKD
rules.description: Detects execution of LiveKD based on PE metadata or image name
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Kernel Memory Dump Via LiveKD
rules.description: Detects execution of LiveKD with the "-m" flag to potentially dump the kernel memory
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Procdump Execution
rules.description: Detects usage of the SysInternals Procdump utility
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential SysInternals ProcDump Evasion
rules.description: Detects uses of the SysInternals ProcDump utility in which ProcDump or its output get renamed, or a dump file is moved or copied to a different name
rules.detection_summary: {'selection_1': {'CommandLine|contains': ['copy procdump', 'move procdump']}, 'selection_2': {'CommandLine|contains|all': ['copy ', '.dmp '], 'CommandLine|contains': ['2.dmp', 'lsass', 'out.dmp']}, 'selection_3': {'CommandLine|contains': ['copy lsass.exe_', 'move lsass.exe_']}, 'condition': '1 of selection_*'}
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential LSASS Process Dump Via Procdump
rules.description:
Detects potential credential harvesting attempts through LSASS memory dumps using ProcDump.
This rule identifies suspicious command-line patterns that combine memory dump flags (-ma, -mm, -mp) with LSASS-related process markers.
LSASS (Local Security Authority Subsystem Service) contains sensitive authentication data including plaintext passwords, NTLM hashes, and Kerberos tickets in memory.
Attackers commonly dump LSASS memory to extract credentials for lateral movement and privilege escalation
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Psexec Execution
rules.description: Detects user accept agreement execution in psexec commandline
rules.author: omkar72

rules.title: PsExec/PAExec Escalation to LOCAL SYSTEM
rules.description: Detects suspicious commandline flags used by PsExec and PAExec to escalate a command line to LOCAL_SYSTEM rights
rules.detection_summary: {'selection_sys': {'CommandLine|contains|windash': [' -s cmd', ' -s -i cmd', ' -i -s cmd', ' -s pwsh', ' -s -i pwsh', ' -i -s pwsh', ' -s powershell', ' -s -i powershell', ' -i -s powershell']}, 'selection_other': {'CommandLine|contains': ['psexec', 'paexec', 'accepteula']}, 'condition': 'all of selection_*'}
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential PsExec Remote Execution
rules.description: Detects potential psexec command that initiate execution on a remote systems via common commandline flags used by the utility
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PsExec Service Execution
rules.description: Detects launch of the PSEXESVC service, which means that this system was the target of a psexec remote execution
rules.author: Thomas Patzke, Romaissa Adjailia, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PsExec Service Child Process Execution as LOCAL SYSTEM
rules.description: Detects suspicious launch of the PSEXESVC service on this system and a sub process run as LOCAL_SYSTEM (-s), which means that someone remotely started a command on this system running it with highest privileges and not only the privileges of the login user account (e.g. the administrator account)
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Use of PsLogList
rules.description: Detects usage of the PsLogList utility to dump event log in order to extract admin accounts and perform account discovery or delete events logs
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Sysinternals PsService Execution
rules.description: Detects usage of Sysinternals PsService which can be abused for service reconnaissance and tampering
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Sysinternals PsSuspend Execution
rules.description: Detects usage of Sysinternals PsSuspend which can be abused to suspend critical processes
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Sysinternals PsSuspend Suspicious Execution
rules.description: Detects suspicious execution of Sysinternals PsSuspend, where the utility is used to suspend critical processes such as AV or EDR to bypass defenses
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential File Overwrite Via Sysinternals SDelete
rules.description: Detects the use of SDelete to erase a file not the free space
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Potential Privilege Escalation To LOCAL SYSTEM
rules.description: Detects unknown program using commandline flags usually used by tools such as PsExec and PAExec to start programs with SYSTEM Privileges
rules.detection_summary: {'selection': {'CommandLine|contains|windash': [' -s cmd', ' -s -i cmd', ' -i -s cmd', ' -s pwsh', ' -s -i pwsh', ' -i -s pwsh', ' -s powershell', ' -s -i powershell', ' -i -s powershell']}, 'filter_main_exclude_coverage': {'CommandLine|contains': ['paexec', 'PsExec', 'accepteula']}, 'condition': 'selection and not 1 of filter_main_*'}
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Sysmon Configuration Update
rules.description: Detects updates to Sysmon's configuration. Attackers might update or replace the Sysmon configuration with a bare bone one to avoid monitoring without shutting down the service completely
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Uninstall Sysinternals Sysmon
rules.description: Detects the removal of Sysmon, which could be a potential attempt at defense evasion
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Potential Binary Impersonating Sysinternals Tools
rules.description:
Detects binaries that use the same name as legitimate sysinternals tools to evade detection.
This rule looks for the execution of binaries that are named similarly to Sysinternals tools.
Adversary may rename their malicious tools as legitimate Sysinternals tools to evade detection.
rules.author: frack113, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Sysprep on AppData Folder
rules.description: Detects suspicious sysprep process start with AppData folder as target (as used by Trojan Syndicasec in Thrip report by Symantec)
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Execution of Systeminfo
rules.description: Detects usage of the "systeminfo" command to retrieve information
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Potential Signing Bypass Via Windows Developer Features
rules.description: Detects when a user enable developer features such as "Developer Mode" or "Application Sideloading". Which allows the user to install untrusted packages.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Recursive Takeown
rules.description: Adversaries can interact with the DACLs using built-in Windows commands takeown which can grant adversaries higher permissions on specific files and folders
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Tap Installer Execution
rules.description: Well-known TAP software installation. Possible preparation for data exfiltration using tunneling techniques
rules.detection_summary: {'selection': {'Image|endswith': '\\tapinstall.exe'}, 'filter_optional_avast': {'Image|contains': [':\\Program Files\\Avast Software\\SecureLine VPN\\', ':\\Program Files (x86)\\Avast Software\\SecureLine VPN\\']}, 'filter_optional_openvpn': {'Image|contains': ':\\Program Files\\OpenVPN Connect\\drivers\\tap\\'}, 'filter_optional_protonvpn': {'Image|contains': ':\\Program Files (x86)\\Proton Techn
rules.author: Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Ian Davis, oscd.community

rules.title: Compressed File Creation Via Tar.EXE
rules.description:
Detects execution of "tar.exe" in order to create a compressed file.
Adversaries may abuse various utilities to compress or encrypt data before exfiltration.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), AdmU3

rules.title: Compressed File Extraction Via Tar.EXE
rules.description:
Detects execution of "tar.exe" in order to extract compressed file.
Adversaries may abuse various utilities in order to decompress data to avoid detection.
rules.author: AdmU3

rules.title: Taskkill Symantec Endpoint Protection
rules.description:
Detects one of the possible scenarios for disabling Symantec Endpoint Protection.
Symantec Endpoint Protection antivirus software services incorrectly implement the protected service mechanism.
As a result, the NT AUTHORITY/SYSTEM user can execute the taskkill /im command several times ccSvcHst.exe /f, thereby killing the process belonging to the service, and thus shutting down the service.
rules.author: Ilya Krestinichev, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Loaded Module Enumeration Via Tasklist.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the enumeration of a specific DLL or EXE being used by a binary via "tasklist.exe".
This is often used by attackers in order to find the specific process identifier (PID) that is using the DLL in question.
In order to dump the process memory or perform other nefarious actions.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

rules.title: Taskmgr as LOCAL_SYSTEM
rules.description: Detects the creation of taskmgr.exe process in context of LOCAL_SYSTEM
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: New Process Created Via Taskmgr.EXE
rules.description: Detects the creation of a process via the Windows task manager. This might be an attempt to bypass UAC
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Command Targeting Teams Sensitive Files
rules.description:
Detects a commandline containing references to the Microsoft Teams database or cookies files from a process other than Teams.
The database might contain authentication tokens and other sensitive information about the logged in accounts.
rules.author: @SerkinValery

rules.title: New Virtual Smart Card Created Via TpmVscMgr.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "Tpmvscmgr.exe" to create a new virtual smart card.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious TSCON Start as SYSTEM
rules.description: Detects a tscon.exe start as LOCAL SYSTEM
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious RDP Redirect Using TSCON
rules.description: Detects a suspicious RDP session redirect using tscon.exe
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential RDP Session Hijacking Activity
rules.description: Detects potential RDP Session Hijacking activity on Windows systems
rules.author: @juju4

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using ChangePK and SLUI
rules.description: Detects an UAC bypass that uses changepk.exe and slui.exe (UACMe 61)
rules.author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using Disk Cleanup
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using scheduled tasks and variable expansion of cleanmgr.exe (UACMe 34)
rules.author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Bypass UAC via CMSTP
rules.description: Detect commandline usage of Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer (cmstp.exe) to install specially formatted local .INF files
rules.author: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community

rules.title: Use of UltraVNC Remote Access Software
rules.description: An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software,to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Suspicious UltraVNC Execution
rules.description: Detects suspicious UltraVNC command line flag combination that indicate a auto reconnect upon execution, e.g. startup (as seen being used by Gamaredon threat group)
rules.author: Bhabesh Raj

rules.title: Uninstall Crowdstrike Falcon Sensor
rules.description: Adversaries may disable security tools to avoid possible detection of their tools and activities by uninstalling Crowdstrike Falcon
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: User Shell Folders Registry Modification via CommandLine
rules.description:
Detects modifications to User Shell Folders registry values via reg.exe or PowerShell, which could indicate persistence attempts.
Attackers may modify User Shell Folders registry values to point to malicious executables or scripts that will be executed during startup.
This technique is often used to maintain persistence on a compromised system by ensuring that malicious payloads are executed automatically.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Uncommon Userinit Child Process
rules.description: Detects uncommon "userinit.exe" child processes, which could be a sign of uncommon shells or login scripts used for persistence.
rules.author: Tom Ueltschi (@c_APT_ure), Tim Shelton

rules.title: Windows Credential Manager Access via VaultCmd
rules.description: List credentials currently stored in Windows Credential Manager via the native Windows utility vaultcmd.exe
rules.author: frack113

rules.title: Registry Modification Attempt Via VBScript
rules.description:
Detects attempts to modify the registry using VBScript's CreateObject("Wscript.shell") and RegWrite methods via common LOLBINs.
It could be an attempt to modify the registry for persistence without using straightforward methods like regedit.exe, reg.exe, or PowerShell.
Threat Actors may use this technique to evade detection by security solutions that monitor for direct registry modifications through traditional tools.
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Verclsid.exe Runs COM Object
rules.description: Detects when verclsid.exe is used to run COM object via GUID
rules.detection_summary: {'selection_img': [{'Image|endswith': '\\verclsid.exe'}, {'OriginalFileName': 'verclsid.exe'}], 'selection_cli': {'CommandLine|contains|all': ['/S', '/C']}, 'filter_main_runtimebroker': {'ParentImage|endswith': 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\RuntimeBroker.exe', 'CommandLine|contains|all': ['verclsid.exe" /S /C {', '} /I {']}, 'condition': 'all of selection_* and not 1 of filter_main_*'}
rules.author: Victor Sergeev, oscd.community

rules.title: Virtualbox Driver Installation or Starting of VMs
rules.description: Adversaries can carry out malicious operations using a virtual instance to avoid detection. This rule is built to detect the registration of the Virtualbox driver or start of a Virtualbox VM.
rules.author: Janantha Marasinghe

rules.title: Suspicious VBoxDrvInst.exe Parameters
rules.description:
Detect VBoxDrvInst.exe run with parameters allowing processing INF file.
This allows to create values in the registry and install drivers.
For example one could use this technique to obtain persistence via modifying one of Run or RunOnce registry keys
rules.author: Konstantin Grishchenko, oscd.community

rules.description: Detects execution of the "VMwareToolBoxCmd.exe" with the "script" and "set" flag to setup a specific script to run for a specific VM state

rules.title: VMToolsd Suspicious Child Process
rules.description: Detects suspicious child process creations of VMware Tools process which may indicate persistence setup
rules.author: bohops, Bhabesh Raj

rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), citron_ninja

rules.title: Visual Studio Code Tunnel Shell Execution

rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Renamed Visual Studio Code Tunnel Execution
rules.description: Detects renamed Visual Studio Code tunnel execution. Attackers can abuse this functionality to establish a C2 channel
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Binary Proxy Execution Via VSDiagnostics.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "VSDiagnostics.exe" with the "start" command in order to launch and proxy arbitrary binaries.
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Proxy Execution via Vshadow
rules.description:
Detects the invocation of vshadow.exe with the -exec parameter that executes a specified script or command after the shadow copies are created but before the VShadow tool exits.
VShadow is a command-line tool that you can use to create and manage volume shadow copies. While legitimate backup or administrative scripts may use this flag,
attackers can leverage this parameter to proxy the execution of malware.
rules.author: David Faiss

rules.title: Suspicious Vsls-Agent Command With AgentExtensionPath Load
rules.description: Detects Microsoft Visual Studio vsls-agent.exe lolbin execution with a suspicious library load using the --agentExtensionPath parameter
rules.author: bohops

rules.title: Vulnerable Driver Blocklist Registry Tampering Via CommandLine
rules.description:
Detects tampering of the Vulnerable Driver Blocklist registry via command line tools such as PowerShell or REG.EXE.
The Vulnerable Driver Blocklist is a security feature that helps prevent the loading of known vulnerable drivers.
Disabling this feature may indicate an attempt to bypass security controls, often targeted by threat actors
to facilitate the installation of malicious or vulnerable drivers, particularly in scenarios involving Endpoint Detection and Response
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Use of W32tm as Timer
rules.description: When configured with suitable command line arguments, w32tm can act as a delay mechanism
rules.author: frack113

rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: All Backups Deleted Via Wbadmin.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the deletion of all backups or system state backups via "wbadmin.exe".
This technique is used by numerous ransomware families and actors.
This may only be successful on server platforms that have Windows Backup enabled.
rules.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Sensitive File Dump Via Wbadmin.EXE

rules.title: File Recovery From Backup Via Wbadmin.EXE

Attackers can restore sensitive files such as NTDS.DIT or Registry Hives from backups in order to potentially extract credentials.

This technique is used by tools such as EDR-Freeze and WSASS to bypass PPL protections and access sensitive information or disable security software.

- WSASS usage typically shows: "WSASS.exe WerFaultSecure.exe [PID]" in ParentCommandLine
- EDR-Freeze usage typically shows: "EDR-Fr
